    • SYSTEMS

    Classic Gold Generation

    League Classic has higher stakes and is generally more snowbally than Season 2026 and that's intentional. We also want players to have a fighting chance at comebacks without adding systems like Objective Bounties that players have to identify and play around. We also don't want to inflate total gold in the game too heavily.

    So we're raising the floor on passive gold income and reducing the income of those who farm the best. As a whole, these changes will result in all champions having about 215 more gold passively, with the average laner roughly treading water.

  • Start of Ambient Gold Generation: 65 seconds ⇒ 90 seconds
  • Passive Gold Per 5 Seconds: 8 / 10.5 / 11.5 / 13 at 1 / 10 / 15 / 25 minutes ⇒ 10.5 / 11.5 / 13 at 1 / 15 / 25 minutes
  • Melee Minion Base Gold Value: 20 ⇒ 19
  • Ranged Minion Base Gold Value: 15 ⇒ 14

    • Classic Homeguards

    We want the early game to have high stakes but that doesn't mean a single kill should spell doom for the next 30 minutes straight. As a result, there's a careful balance to strike between properly rewarding the victor for an early kill and helping losing players have something to look forward to. One of our attempts to strike that balance was early game Homeguards, which shipped with Classic last patch. This moderate 10% move speed buff should only shave a second or two off of someone's walk back to lane but your feedback that it feels too modern has been heard. We're keeping the mid-game version of Homeguard, which exists to help winning teams cross the map and continue sieging, but the early game one is being removed. In its place, we're reducing early game death timers by a couple seconds. No new mechanics to learn and winners still get ahead, but losers can get back in there and earn XP and gold to look for their comeback.

  • Homeguard Activation: 0 minutes ⇒ 15 minutes
  • Death Timers: 12 / 14 / 16 / 19 / 22 / 25 / 28 / 30 ⇒ 10 / 12 / 14 / 17 / 20 / 23 / 26 / 29 (levels 1-8)
  • Death Timers At Levels 9+: Unchanged ⇒ Unchanged

    • Classic Jungle Tuning

    When porting over jungle monsters to modern systems, we miscalculated how durable regular jungle monsters would become in the mid and late game. This global health scaling buff will make camps more closely match their histories. Your first clear won't be affected at all, and non-epic monsters will scale up to 5-25% more health than they had before.

  • Maximum Health Scaling: 250% ⇒ 315%

    • Classic Turrets

    Despite having the same effective HP they had in 2013, player feedback has been overwhelming that turrets feel too squishy. And they're certainly much frailer than 2026's norms. As we want turrets to matter and feel important, we agree that they could stand to hold up better, so we're buffing their health by around 15% across the board and nerfing the AP ratio to on-hit damage conversion against towers.

    • Arena

    Hey Arenaheads! This Arena patch comes with many champion balance changes, primarily bringing up those that have been struggling for a while so that they get their chance in the spotlight, along with tapping down a few of the most dominant champions.

    As for some exciting highlights, Rek'Sai's tunnels will have a 0 second used cooldown when maxed, allowing for some rapid in and out gameplay, Gnar's tired time is being removed so that you're constantly swapping back and forth, and Now You See Me level 2 spawns a clone where you vanished from.

    Last but definitely not least, we're bringing back Bravery Arena! For the foreseeable future, Arena will be embracing Bravery and Crowd Favorites every Wednesday. For those that didn't get the chance to play during Bravery weekends, here's the rundown: On Wednesdays, each player will only be able to select Bravery, or choose from their pool of Crowd Favorite champions. The number of Crowd Favorites you're offered is based on how many champions you own.

    We know that while a lot of people love Bravery, others enjoy picking from their pool of favorite champions. Our hope is that by having Bravery and Crowd Favorites at a consistent time players will be able to plan when they play to get the experience they are looking for, as well as being open to experimenting with new builds they might not have tried yet.

entries.text: Reduced the volume of base Locke (Q) missile cast sound effects to better sit in the overall game mix.
Fixed a bug where Viego with the Bot lane Role Quest would be able to steal his possessed target's boots.
Fixed a bug where upgrading from Hexdrinker to Maw of Malmortius did not reset the cooldown of the item.
Fixed a bug where killing a ward would display debug text for spectators.
Fixed a bug where Locke picking up his (R) artifact would refund based on its current cooldown instead of the total cooldown.
Fixed a bug where in certain circumstances Taunt and Berserk effects could be ignored using WASD controls.
Fixed a bug where Support players' Control wards would be consumed when trying to place them while dead.
Fixed a bug where Ambessa's omnivamp would apply on turrets when driving Rift Herald into them.
Fixed a bug where Mordekaiser (R) improperly gains Ability Haste.
Fixed a bug where Bel'Veth's resource bar would incorrectly update if she hit 80 stacks while already in True Form.
Fixed a bug where Locke (R) execution would be considered a spell cast.
Fixed a bug where Viktor (R) lightning VFX would stretch across the screen in certain situations.

html:
In 26.17 we’ve got a small amount of relief for top lane with Nasus and Vayne nerfs, and some followup on last patch to a handful of champions and items. We’re buffing a variety of melee AD carries, like Irelia, Qiyana, Yasuo, and Yone, who’ve been forced to snowball-or-lose for a while instead of having a reliable endgame to scale towards. Xerath continues to overperform in the mid lane in particular, as do Nocturne and Graves in the jungle. Finally, Sundered Sky wasn’t hit quite as hard as we were looking for, and we’re also looking to give Stormrazor a place in some builds again.

Looking for more information on all things League of Legends? Check out our community-run wiki here!

Wrong patch notes? You can find the TFT patch notes here!

Patch Highlights

Heartsong Seraphine, Ocean Song Soraka, and Ocean Song Jinx will be available August 26, 2026.

Champions

Aurelion Sol

Aurelion Sol has come out the loser of last patch's mage adjustments, so we are giving him a buff to help him out. In particular, we are buffing his W cooldown so he can use it a bit more freely rather than only when a reset is likely. This should also make it a bit more clear to players that W is typically the stronger second skill to max, rather than E. 

Q - Breath of Light

  • Mana Cost Per Second: 35 / 40 / 45 / 50 / 55 ⇒ 30 / 35 / 40 / 45 / 50

    • W - Astral Flight

  • Cooldown: 22 / 20.5 / 19 / 17.5 / 16s ⇒ 22 / 20 / 18 / 16 / 14s

    • Cho'Gath

    Cho's early game has lost pizzazz with Hail of Blades and Hextech Rocketbelt nerfs, so we are making it up with a bit of early damage when he does get those autos off.

    E - Vorpal Spikes

  • Base Damage (x3 attacks): 20 / 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 (+30% AP) (+2.5% - 3.9% (+.5% Per Feast) Target Max HP) ⇒ 30 / 50 / 70 / 90 / 110 (+30% AP) (+2.5% - 3.9% (+.5% Per Feast) Target Max HP)

    • Graves

    Graves has had a number of indirect buffs over the last few patches and this has put him in a pretty strong spot. We are looking to soften a bit of his ability to snowball the game with high AD builds. 

    Q - End of the Line

  • Initial Damage: 50 / 75 / 100 / 125 / 150 (+65% bonus AD) ⇒ 50 / 75 / 100 / 125 / 150 (+55% bonus AD)
  • Return Damage: 80 / 125 / 170 / 215 / 260 (+55 / 70 / 85 / 100 / 115% bonus AD) ⇒ 80 / 125 / 170 / 215 / 260 (+45 / 60 / 75 / 90 / 105% bonus AD)

    • Irelia

    Irelia is one of League’s highest stakes snowballing dependant skirmishers, but we feel like even when ahead she is failing to scale into a real carry threat

    Q - Bladesurge

  • Damage: 5 / 25 / 45 / 65 / 85 (+70% AD) ⇒ 5 / 25 / 45 / 65 / 85 (+80% AD)

    • Additionally, we are buffing some of her AP ratios to support wacky ARAM/Arena builds. We don’t expect this to make AP Irelia suddenly good for SR.

    W - Defiant Dance

  • Damage Reduction Ability Power Ratio: 7% per 100 AP (Halved for Magic Damage) (reduced to 75% value for Magic Damage in Arena) ⇒ 8% per 100 AP (Halved for Magic Damage) (reduced to 75% value for Magic Damage in Arena)

    • R - Vanguard's Edge

  • Ability Power Ratio: 70% ⇒ 100% (It is already 100% in Arena, so this is standardizing the value)

    • LeBlanc

    With the previous version of Statikk Shiv that drove nerfing her AS ratios no longer in the game, we’re bringing these closer to a typical champion’s baseline. Simultaneously, having some room for power, we are giving her some AP ratio buffs to make sure she's still interested primarily in AP assassination builds.

    Base Stats

  • Attack Speed Ratio: 0.4 ⇒ 0.625
  • Attack Speed Growth: 2.35% ⇒ 1.5%

    • W - Distortion

  • Damage: 75 / 115 / 155 / 195 / 235 (+80% AP) ⇒ 75 / 115 / 155 / 195 / 235 (+90% AP)

    • RW - Mimic: Distortion

  • Damage: 150 / 315 / 480 (+80% AP) ⇒ 150 / 315 / 480 (+90% AP)

    • Nasus

    Nasus top has been able to benefit from the shift in his stacking paradigm. We are happy to see our favorite dog get his fill of treats, but want to make sure that we keep his power within reasonable bounds, therefore we are going to be tapping down some of Nasus' top specific strengths, like persistently lifestealing off of minions.

    Passive - Soul Eater

  • Life Steal: 12 / 18 / 24% ⇒ 10 / 15 / 20%

    • Nocturne

    Nocturne has been sitting in a pretty strong state across skill levels for a while. We are excited about the opportunities that open up when Nocturne unlocks his ult, but want to add a bit more personal risk to him accessing that high moment.

    Base Stats

  • Armor: 38 ⇒ 36
  • Health: 655 ⇒ 640

    • Qiyana

    Qiyana's play has moved out of primarily mid to jungle. While we are happy to support her as a jungler, mid is where she’s been underwhelming recently .

    Q - Elemental Wrath

  • Damage: 70 / 100 / 130 / 160 / 190 (+85% bonus AD) ⇒ 80 / 110 / 140 / 170 / 200 (+90% bonus AD)
  • Monster Damage Modifier: 175% against Monsters ⇒ 160% against Monsters

    • Thresh

    Thresh has been quietly sitting at a high winrate and picking up playrate over the year.

    E - Flay

  • Active Damage: 75 / 120 / 165 / 210 / 255 (+70% AP) ⇒ 65 / 110 / 155 / 200 / 245 (+60% AP)

    • Trundle

    Sometimes you just wanna club your opponents to death, and while Trundle has been a resilient utility pick for his pillar and ult, we feel his personal clubbing power has actually been a bit limp.

    W - Frozen Domain

  • Attack Speed: 30 / 45 / 60 / 75 / 90% ⇒ 30 / 50 / 70 / 90 / 110%

    • Vayne

    We believe Vayne may need larger scope work in the future to help out her bot lane, but for now are prioritizing constraining her top lane power. These changes should impact her up there more than in bot lane.

    Base Stats

  • Health: 550 + 103/Level ⇒ 580 + 98/Level
  • Health Regeneration: 3.5 + .55/Level ⇒ 4 + .5/Level
  • Attack Speed Ratio: .658 + 3.3%/Level ⇒ .67 + 2.8%/Level

    • Q - Tumble

  • Mana Cost: 30 ⇒ 46 / 42 / 38 / 34 / 30

    • W - Silver Bolts

  • True Damage: 6 / 7 / 8 / 9 / 10% Target Max HP ⇒ 4 / 5.5 / 7 / 8.5 / 10% Target Max HP
  • Minimum Damage: 50 / 65 / 80 / 95 / 110 ⇒ 40 / 55 / 70 / 85 / 100

    • Xerath

    Xerath has rested slightly high in power both mid and bot, and after last patch's adjustments to mages has come out on top in mid lane compared to others. Given his extremely high ban rate in certain regions, he's due a light nerf.

    Base Stats

  • Health: 596 ⇒ 575

    • Q - Arcanopulse

  • Damage: 75 / 115 / 155 / 195 / 235 (+90% AP) ⇒ 70 / 110 / 150 / 190 / 230 (+90% AP)

    • Yasuo

    While Yasuo has definitely been able to snowball and carry games, we believe that similar to Irelia, he is too reliant on snowballing rather than just being a proper scaling carry. We also want to encourage him to prioritize early crit strike builds over Blade of the Ruined King, so we are reducing his crit damage penalty which will simultaneously encourage this as well help him scale without significantly impacting his early game snowball.

    Passive - Way of the Wanderer

  • Critical Strike Damage Reduction: -10% ⇒ -5%

    • Yone

    Similar to Yasuo, Yone has also been an excessively snowball reliant carry, though less so. Bros stay together.

    Passive - Way of the Hunter

  • Critical Strike Damage Reduction: -10% ⇒ -5%

    • Items

    Stormrazor

    Stormrazor almost had its time in the sun earlier this year, but has ended up remaining second fiddle.

  • Attack Speed: 20% ⇒ 25%

    • Sundered Sky

    Last patch’s Sundered Sky nerf was a step in the right direction, but landed a bit under-target given all of the other moving pieces of that patch.

  • Health: 450 ⇒ 400
  • Attack Damage: 45 ⇒ 40

    • Classic

    Our second patch for League Classic contains tons of good stuff! We’re giving everyone two additional Rune Pages, increasing Influence Points and Classic XP gains across the board, and reducing the cost of about one third of the runes. We’re updating Summoner’s Rift’s lighting, textures, and decals to bring our visual fidelity closer to the Rift of old. We’ve also got our first Council vote, so be sure to log in and make your voice heard. Remember that the more Classic you play, the more voting power you can earn! 

    We’ve also got about 20 balance changes, several dozen bugfixes, and have added Champion and Role swapping to Champion Select to improve your day-to-day Classic experience.

    Champions

    Ahri

    Ahri is extremely safe, has good sustain, good wave clear, and the ability to all-in her opponents at a moment's notice. She’s also overpowered. We want to trim some of her extraneous early safety and reduce how frequently she can pressure her opposition.

    Base Stats

  • Base Health Regeneration: 6.1 ⇒ 4.5
  • Health Regeneration Growth: 0.6 ⇒ 0.45
  • Health: 460 ⇒ 440

    • R - Spirit Rush

  • Cooldown: 110 / 95 / 80 ⇒ 120 / 100 / 80

    • Annie

    Annie is our second weakest mid laner behind Lux, so we’re driving on some buffs. We’re first reverting some damage nerfs from July 2011 and otherwise ensuring her offensive threat is up to snuff.

    Passive - Pyromania

  • Stun Duration: 1.5s ⇒ 1.75s

    • Q - Disintegrate

  • Damage: 85 / 125 / 165 / 205 / 245 + 70% AP ⇒ 90 / 130 / 170 / 210 / 250 + 75% AP

    • W - Incinerate

  • Damage: 80 / 130 / 180 / 230 / 280 + 75% AP ⇒ 85 / 135 / 185 / 235 / 285 + 80% AP

    • E - Molten Shield

  • Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where Molten Shield dealt too little damage

  • Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where Molten Shield could damage enemies for non-Attacks 

    R - Summon: Tibbers!

  • Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where AP was not applying to Tibbers’s burn damage.

    • Ashe

    As a supportive ADC, Ashe is performing below average. She’s not massively underpowered, but weak enough to deserve a buff. To do that, we’re reverting a 2010 Volley nerf, letting her succeed more while playing at long ranges, poking and suppressing her opponents from afar.

    W - Volley

  • Damage: 40 / 50 / 60 / 70 / 80 + 100% total AD ⇒ 40 / 55 / 70 / 85 / 100 + 100% total AD
  • Range: 1200 ⇒ 1300

    • Blitzcrank

    Blitzcrank is due for much larger nerfs than they got last patch, so we’re back to bring the highest agency support in the game down to size. We’re continuing to revisit old patches to return older, weaker tuning. We’re also fixing a few bugs and oversights to bring their power down further. Our one unique contribution is a rank 1 and 2 nerf to Static Field’s active. Combined with the cooldown nerf, we hope that Blitzcrank players will occasionally choose to keep the R in its passive form, playing for a more sustained damage threat.

    Passive - Mana Barrier

  • Tooltip: Clarifies that Mana Barrier only pops if Blitzcrank is below 20% Health when taking damage.
  • Shield: 50% maximum mana ⇒ 50% current mana

    • Q - Rocket Grab

  • Range: 1080 ⇒ 1050
  • Mana Cost: 120 ⇒ 140

    • E - Power Fist

  • Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where the cooldown was always 5 seconds, regardless of rank or Cooldown Reduction.
  • Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where the target was stunned for approximately 0.3 seconds longer than intended.

    • R - Static Field

  • Active Damage: 200 / 300 / 400 ⇒ 150 / 275 / 400
  • Cooldown: 30s ⇒ 40s

    • Dr. Mundo

    Dr. Mundo’s still in need of some extra healthcare even after last patch’s buffs as one of the worst top laners and junglers in the game. We’re back with further increases to his durability, in hopes of making him the biggest meat wall you’ve ever seen. His health buffs come from reverts to nerfs in April of 2011. We’re also handing him some extra early game attack speed, which is meant to disproportionately buff his jungling, where he currently performs worse than in top lane.

    Base Stats

  • Health: 522 ⇒ 560
  • Health Growth: 89 ⇒ 90
  • Level 1 Attack Speed: 0.625 ⇒ 0.658

    • Evelynn

    Evelynn is one of the best-performing junglers in Classic and is gaining more win rate over time as players learn how to optimize her. As such, she’s due for a nerf. We’re pulling a mix of reverted buffs from her initial release and nerfs from 2013’s future. We're making Dark Frenzy worse when just spammed to get across the map, reducing her mid-late jungle clear speed, and making her consider her mana costs more, just like other AP junglers.

    Passive - Shadow Walk

  • Maximum Mana Regeneration While Camouflaged: 1% ⇒ 0.8%

    • Q - Hate Spike

  • Base Damage: 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 / 120 ⇒ 40 / 55 / 70 / 85 / 100
  • Missile Speed: 3000 - 800, decaying ⇒ 2000 - 800, decaying

    • W - Dark Frenzy

  • Mana Cost: 0 ⇒ 40
  • Cooldown: 15s ⇒ 20s

    • Ezreal

    As players have sanded off the rust, Ezreal has moved to the top of the pile as the most picked bot laner by far and too strong a performer considering his high degree of safety. As this dominance is driven by AD Ezreal, we’re delivering some compensation changes to keep AP Ezreal afloat as well. Our nerfs are a tour of changes from back in June of 2010, picking up two Q nerfs and reverting an R nerf from 16 years ago.

    Q - Mystic Shot

  • Total Attack Damage Ratio: 120% ⇒ 110%
  • Cast Range: 1200 ⇒ 1100

    • R - Trueshot Barrage

  • Ability Power Ratio: 70% ⇒ 100%

    • Garen

    We were conservative with many of our changes last patch, which has left Garen still in a very weak position. We’re back to deliver much stronger buffs with the goal of bringing him up to speed. We have two primary goals with our buffs. The first is to ensure that spin-to-win always feels rewarding, especially early game. The other is to ensure that he feels good about all his item purchases, whether scaling his damage or durability.

    Base Stats

  • Attack Damage: 55.5 ⇒ 60
  • Armor Growth: 2.7 ⇒ 3

    • W - Courage

  • Bonus Armor and Magic Resistance Increase: 20% ⇒ 30%

    • E - Judgment

  • Damage Per Second: 20 / 45 / 70 / 95 / 120 + 70 / 80 / 90 / 100 / 110% total AD ⇒ 20 / 45 / 70 / 95 / 120 + 80 / 90 / 100 / 110 / 120% total AD

    • Gragas

    Gragas is extremely safe, very bursty, and overall just overperforms in mid lane. Our nerfs are aimed at making him less safe as a laner and make him consider his openings more carefully without reducing his burst damage by much.

    Q - Barrel Roll

  • Cooldown: 11.5 / 10.5 / 9.5 / 8.5 / 7.5s ⇒ 12.5 / 11.5 / 10.5 / 9.5 / 8.5s
  • Damage: 85 / 135 / 185 / 235 / 285 + 90% AP ⇒ 75 / 125 / 175 / 225 / 275 + 90% AP

    • W - Drunken Rage

  • Cooldown: 25s ⇒ 30s

    • R - Explosive Cask

  • Cooldown: 100 / 90 / 80s ⇒ 130 / 115 / 100s

    • Heimerdinger

    Heimerdinger is on the strong side, even after last patch’s nerfs. He’s got a meaningful bugfix this patch, so we wanted to call it out directly.

    W - Hextech Micro-Rockets

  • Range Display: Now accurately displays the actual missile range.

    • R - UPGRADE!!!

  • Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where R-empowered turrets dealt double damage.

    • Jax

    Jax is receiving a few bug fixes this patch, and while he’s pretty balanced, they’re important enough changes to warrant being called out on their own.

    Q - Leap Strike

  • Damage Type: Physical ⇒ Magic

    • R - Relentless Assault

  • Ability Name: Grandmaster’s Might ⇒ Relentless Assault
  • Spell Effects: Now applies spell effects as a single-target spell.

    • Kayle

    When we launched Kayle in League Classic, we chose one of her earliest kits, which included gaining bonus AD from AP and vice versa. This version of the kit never allowed her to remain permanently ranged with enough CDR, as that buff only came in with her next rework. Ultimately, we like this version of the kit but think she should be able to be permanently ranged if she builds for it, so we’re buffing E’s cooldown. You’ll need at least 38% CDR at rank 5 to hit that breakpoint, so enjoy your build goals!

    E - Righteous Fury

  • Cooldown: 22 / 21 / 20 / 19 / 18s ⇒ 20 / 19 / 18 / 17 / 16s

    • Lux

    Lux is still performing worse than she ought to so we’re back with some more buffs. We’re increasing Lucent Singularity’s radius to its old wide self as another callback to the past. We’re also bringing in some modern touches (or, farther back in the past depending on how you look at it), including some bug fixes. We’re letting her use summoner spells and detonate her E during her R cast. Flashing will not change the hit location, but you can dodge an Ashe arrow if you need to. 

    We’re also giving her better defensive immediacy. It’s important that League is responsive to your inputs, and “Shield me!” is about as immediate a need as it gets. This is one modernization that we think is very important to give Lux even in this older version of the game. 

    We’re also starting our adventure into new territory here. One of Classic’s biggest strengths is the wide-open space for build experimentation. We’d like if Lux could be part of that space. For anyone playing a more conventional AP Lux playstyle, this attack speed should still help her to last hit minions or pop Illumination stacks between spells more quickly. Or… You could be adventurous and try AD Lux, or maybe AP on-hit Lux with a Malady and a Nashor’s Tooth. You know you want to.

    Base Stats

  • Attack Speed Growth: 1.36% ⇒ 3%
  • Attack Speed Ratio: 0.625 ⇒ 0.658 (Level 1 Attack Speed unchanged)

    • W - Prismatic Barrier

  • Shield Timing: The shield now comes out at the start of the cast, instead of at the end. Total cast time unchanged.

    • E - Lucent Singularity

  • Radius: 310 ⇒ 350
  • Cast Interaction: E may now be detonated while casting R.

    • R - Final Spark

  • Cast Interaction: Lux may now use summoner spells and items while casting R. Flash will not change the location of the beam.
  • Cooldown: No longer goes on cooldown if Lux dies while casting it.

    • Miss Fortune

    Miss Fortune’s buffs last patch didn’t go nearly far enough, so we’re back for more. Once again we’re digging up changes of old, undoing almost every nerf she received since her launch and fixing several bugs that could cause her ultimate to not deliver on expectations. We’re also delivering one novel change to make E’s mana cost respect its rank, so it’ll be cheaper at low investment and more expensive (and more powerful) when maxed.

    Base Stats

  • Move Speed: 325 ⇒ 335

    • Q - Double Up

  • Damage: 25 / 60 / 95 / 130 / 165 + 75% total AD ⇒ 35 / 70 / 105 / 140 / 175 + 75% total AD. Secondary target still takes 120% of the damage.
  • Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where Double Up could fail to bounce.

    • E - Make It Rain

  • Total Damage: 90 / 145 / 200 / 255 / 310 ⇒ 95 / 155 / 215 / 275 / 335
  • Slow Duration: 0.25s ⇒ 1s. Refresh rate unchanged.
  • Mana Cost: 80 ⇒ 70 / 75 / 80 / 85 / 90

    • R - Bullet Time

  • Damage Per Wave: 65 / 95 / 125 + 40% bonus AD + 20% AP ⇒ 65 / 95 / 125 + 45% bonus AD + 30% AP
  • Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where Miss Fortune could fail to shoot all 8 waves.
  • Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where Bullet Time could fail to damage an enemy all 8 times.

    • Sivir

    Sivir currently lacks a strong strategic niche or high point to her experience. Toggled Ricochet is meant to be an extremely potent output that Sivir players should feel great about, so we’re reverting some nerfs to it from back in January 2011.

    Passive - Fleet of Foot

  • Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where the movement speed could be gained by attacking minions.

    • W - Ricochet

  • Bounce Radius: 450 ⇒ 500
  • Damage Falloff: 25% ⇒ 22%

    • Tristana

    Tristana is clearly a peak performer in bot lane while mid lane AP Tristana in mid is doing just fine, so we’re taking aim at AD-specific Tristana nerfs to her attack speed. Her mana growth compensation is meant to mostly compensate mid Tristana for the small amount of collateral damage she’s receiving.

    Base Stats

  • Attack Speed Growth: 4% ⇒ 3%
  • Mana Growth: 32 ⇒ 40

    • Q - Rapid Fire

  • Mana Cost: 50 ⇒ 50 / 60 / 70 / 80 / 90

    • Tryndamere

    Tryndamere is still doing exceptionally well. After calibrating how impactful our changes would be in the first patch, we’re back to put him where he belongs. Somehow, he has even more buffs from back in 2010 that we can revert, so we’re back to make things tougher on him. We’re also doing some unique changes, namely reducing his early resilience to losing lane. The primary nerf, however, is in reducing his top-end crit chance. For those with at least 3 crit items, Tryndamere will still be able to reach 100% crit chance at low health, but in the early and mid game, he won’t crit as often.

    Base Stats

  • Base Health Regeneration: 10 ⇒ 7.5
  • Health Regeneration Growth: 0.9 ⇒ 0.75

    • Passive - Battle Fury

  • Maximum Critical Strike Chance: 50% ⇒ 30%
  • Maximum Critical Strike Chance Reached At: 0% Health ⇒ 5% Health

    • R - Undying Rage

  • Cooldown: 110 / 100 / 90s ⇒ 130 / 115 / 100s

    • Twitch

    Twitch’s nerfs from last patch didn’t do enough to dethrone him from the top spot. We’re taking out a mix of damage and durability, ultimately trying to make sure that his damage output is readable when exiting out of stealth.

    Base Stats

  • Base Attack Speed: 0.679 ⇒ 0.658
  • Level 1 Attack Speed: 0.679 ⇒ 0.658
  • Health: 470 ⇒ 455

    • Items

    Innervating Locket

    When we remade Innervating Locket in Classic, we preemptively nerfed it, as it had been removed from the game for being unbalanceable. Well, it turns out, it’s possible to make it too weak to be used. So we’re here for some meaningful buffs aimed at making it shine for those who want it. We want to make sure it’s an appealing support option, restoring many of the stats it used to have and buffing its unique effect. Innervating Lockets do stack across multiple players, by the way, so if all five of you buy one, you can put a lot of healing onto your most injured teammate.

  • Combine Cost: 750g (2650g total cost) ⇒ 350g (2250g total cost)
  • Health: 430 ⇒ 500
  • Cooldown Reduction: 0% ⇒ 10%
  • Innervation Health and Mana Restored: 50 / 20 ⇒ 60 / 25

    • Wriggle’s Lantern and Feral Flare

    When we built out the items in League Classic, we knew there’d be some conflicts. We had items coexisting who never coexisted before, or were placed into a game that didn’t quite fit. One of these conflicts was with jungle items: We have monster tuning from 2013 (plus the Wight), but have the 2014 item Feral Flare. When we launched, we simply took the 2013 version of Madred’s Razors and Wriggle’s Lantern, and simply updated Feral Flare to fit the same stat profile. 

    We’re changing that now. We’re reshaping Wriggle’s Lantern and Feral Flare to be Attack Speed items instead of Attack Damage ones but keeping all the other stats the same. This change helps them stand out against Spirit of the Elder Lizard, and preserves Hunter’s Machete and Madred’s Razors as they were. These new items do overlap with Madred’s Bloodrazor a bit, but you’re still welcome to buy them both.

  • Build Path: Madred’s Razors + Vampiric Scepter ⇒ Madred’s Razors + Recurve Bow. Total cost (2000g) unchanged.
  • Attack Damage: 25 ⇒ 0
  • Attack Speed: 0% ⇒ 30%

    • Runes and Progression

    We’ve heard your feedback loud and clear about how slow it feels to gain access to runes, games with stakes, and more. So in this patch we have large sweeping buffs to several systems that should have you building out extra rune pages and gaining SP in no time!

  • Rune Pages: Everyone has been given 2 additional Rune Pages for free
  • Influence Points: IP gained per game has more than doubled
  • Classic XP: Classic XP gained per game has doubled
  • Bug Fix: Players no longer gain party XP/IP bonuses when solo queued
  • Quintessence IP Cost: 1250 ⇒ 1000
  • Minor Rune IP Cost: 650 ⇒ 500

    • Quintessence of Health Regeneration

  • Health Regeneration per 5 seconds: +1.5 ⇒ +3.0

    • Systems

    Champion Swapping

    You can now swap champions and roles during Champion Select! So now your first pick mid laner can grab Blitzcrank for you, you can grab AP Shaco for your bot laner, and you can successfully make your opponents rage quit instead of having to dodge..

  •   NEW   Champion Swap: Enabled during the Loadout phase.
  •   NEW   Swap Request: Players can request to swap champions, and players can accept swap requests. Lanes stay the same.
  •   NEW   Champion Pick Order Swapping: Players can swap champion pick order.

    • The Inaugural Council Vote

    The Council goes live with this patch! Vote on the game’s future inside the game client. You will be able to vote on multiple topics during the active voting period and we’ll be back to share the results once voting closes.

  •   NEW   Voting Topics: Players can see and vote on multiple topics during active voting.
  •   NEW   Voting Results: Players can see the results for the topics that were voted on.

    • Ranked Loading Screen Borders

  •   REMOVED   Modern Ranked Borders: Removed from the Classic loading screen.

    • Art

    A few of our artists got together and updated several aspects of Summoner’s Rift to make it look more like the original.

  • Art Updates: Added missing foliage and decals, removed an unintended prop, updated decals and map details, and corrected affected walls, ground, and mesh normals.
  • Lighting Updates: Updated lighting at both spawn locations and on the purple diamond torches to look closer to the original.

    • Bugfixes

  • Fixed a bug where Exhaust reduced true damage.
  • Fixed bugs where Iceborn Gauntlet, Kayle’s Reckoning, and Shaco’s Two-Shiv Poison ignored Master Yi’s Highlander’s slow resistance and Morgana’s Black Shield.
  • Fixed bugs where many spells did not trigger Call for Help and therefore did not provoke minion aggro.
  • Fixed a bug where moving a stacked Tear item over another Tear item could copy the number of stacks to the other Tear items.
  • Fixed a bug where Vayne’s Condemn (E) granted 8 Tear stacks instead of 4.
  • Fixed a bug where placing Red Trinket, Sight Ward, or Vision Ward canceled Recall.
  • Fixed a bug where Statikk Shiv triggered before a ranged projectile landed on an enemy unit.
  • Fixed a bug where Sivir’s Spell Shield (E) did not block Leona’s Zenith Blade (E).
  • Fixed a bug where the client could display an empty content area after the XP Results screen.
  • Fixed bugs where Nidalee’s Bushwhack/Pounce (W) tooltip omitted the trap duration, displayed debug text for Cougar Form damage values, and displayed incorrect spacing and text colors.
  • Fixed a bug where Lulu’s Faerie Companion (Passive) glowing model VFX disappeared after disconnecting and reconnecting.
  • Fixed a bug where Amumu’s Despair (W) VFX disappeared and its SFX remained at Amumu’s last location after disconnecting and reconnecting.
  • Fixed a bug where Leona’s Zenith Blade’s missile hitbox was too narrow.
  • Fixed a bug where Akali’s AD/AP particles were misaligned on her hands for Classic skins.
  • Fixed a bug where Akali’s Q mark did not display its Heal VFX if her passive was active.
  • Fixed a bug where Anivia’s Q tooltip did not show the slow duration.
  • Fixed a bug where Kassadin’s Passive tooltip did not accurately reflect that Kassadin gains Attack Speed based on damage mitigated.
  • Fixed a bug where Lee Sin’s Q tooltip did not clarify its damage cap to monsters.
  • Fixed a bug where Leona’s Q tooltip did not show the accurate stun duration.
  • Fixed a bug where Soraka’s W tooltip did not show the accurate Armor buff duration.
  • Fixed various bugs where tooltip values and ability data were hardcoded instead of referencing the appropriate data values.
  • Fixed a bug where Fiddlesticks’s Dark Wind could interrupt his attack animation every time it bounced
  • Fixed a bug where Amumu’s Bandage Toss didn’t scale with Cooldown Reduction.
  • Fixed a bug where the Strength of Spirit Mastery required players to invest 3 points into Expanded Mind.
  • Fixed a tooltip bug with Energy Regeneration Seals not mentioning that it was per 5 seconds.
  • Fixed multiple text box bugs in the Classic Home Page.
  • Fixed sorting bugs with Portraits in the Classic Store.

    • ARAM: Mayhem

    Hello Mayhemers, in this patch, we’re continuing to focus on the fighter experience. We’re introducing two more fighter Augments: Ultra Hydra and Upgrade Death’s Dance! Three-by-Three-headed Hydra? (Just kidding.) We hope these new options give fighters even more ways to sustain themselves and make a big impact in the middle of a team fight. 

    For Augment adjustments and nerfs, we’re taking a look at some high-frustration ADC Augments that have been both powerful and visually noisy. We’re tuning them down to give opponents more room to react and make team fights easier to read. Double Tap has been changed to Prismatic given its power level. 

    We’ve also made some adjustments to the Augment pool so champions get a selection of options that better fit their playstyles. Let us know how these changes feel, and see you on the Bridge!

    Augments

    Critical Missile

  • Missile Amount: 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 based on crit chance ⇒ 1 / 2 / 3 based on crit chance

    • Double Tap

  • Tier: Gold ⇒ Prismatic

    • Tripleshot

  • Targeting: Now prioritizes enemies nearby the main target

    • Ultra Hydra

  •   NEW   Quest: Gain Ravenous Hydra, Profane Hydra and Titanic Hydra
  •   NEW   Reward: Gain Ultra Hydra

  •   NEW   Effect: Gain 250 Gold. 40%/15% of damage taken is dealt to you over 3 seconds. Heal 125% bonus AD instantly when scoring a takedown.

    • Upgrade Infinity Edge

  •   REMOVED   Critical Strike Chance: Removed

    • Upgrade Ravenous

  • Fixed a bug where Stuck in Here With Me triggers after Mordekaiser’s (R) ended.
  • Fixed a bug where Echo Cast clone will cast spells in the wrong direction after reconnecting.
  • Fixed a bug where Archmage put ammo spells on cooldown when casting other spells.
  • Fixed a bug where teammates' burn and damage over time also grant Gold after Blood Money Burn triggers.
  • Fixed a bug where High Roller failed to trigger on certain champions.

    • Arena

    As Arena reaches a stable place, both with its players and balance we want to continue to hit outliers, we especially want to bring up those that feel like they haven’t had a place in the mode or are a bit too powerful that they are gatekeeping others from finding a home in the mode. 

    Going forward Arena will also be shifting back to an alternating patch schedule, with the plan being to aim for balance patches on odd numbered League of Legends patches. We feel that the mode is generally in a healthy place and we don’t want to be making adjustments so frequently that players feel that their builds and discovery will be balanced out too quickly.

html:
The Beacon of Hope has officially been inducted into the Hall of Legends. Congratulations, Caps!

This week's patch kicks off our event that honors the most decorated player in European League of Legends history. The Hall of Legends battle pass will take you on a journey through his storied career, and features new cosmetics plus brand new skins co-developed by Caps himself. We can't wait to celebrate such a humble, confident, and resilient competitor with you all.

This patch also features changes to Summoner's Rift balance, with some targeted nerfs on overperforming pro supports like Nautilus and Bard, as well as some taps to Seraphine bot and Zeri. A round of buffs is in order for Viego, Zaahen, Master Yi, Ekko, and Kassadin. Finally, Cassiopeia has slithered her way into an adjustment to help reduce her pro skew.

Classic will be having a big old Demacian reunion this week as Fiora, Galio, Poppy, Shyvana, and Xin Zhao join the fray in addition to a host of balance changes and the results of our first Council vote!

For all you Mayhem heads out there, we're making sure that the Augment choices you receive make more sense for the champion you're playing, as we continue to improve the Augment pools.

Looking for more information on all things League of Legends? Check out our community-run wiki here!

Wrong patch notes? You can find the TFT patch notes here!

Patch Highlights

Immortalized Legend Tristana, Risen Legend Orianna, and Risen Legend Tristana will be available September 10, 2026.

Hall of Legends

LoL Esports inducts a pro player into the Hall of Legends to honor their achievements within the sport and game. Players are chosen by an independent voting panel of esports industry veterans and experts from every region who select players based on criteria including international berths, international and regional titles, role-specific stats, and overall contributions to the sport.

We're honored to announce that Rasmus "Caps" Winther is the third inductee into the Hall of Legends! Known as a Beacon of Hope whose legacy reshaped what the West believed was possible on the global stage, Caps becomes the first Western League of Legends pro to earn the distinction.


Widely regarded as the defining Western player of his generation, Caps built his legacy through a rare blend of elite skill, creativity, and authenticity. From his meteoric rise as a rookie to becoming the most decorated player in European League of Legends history, Caps has consistently proven he can stand toe-to-toe with the world's best while staying true to his own style.


The in-game Hall of Legends event pass celebrates Caps' countless accomplishments and takes you on a journey through his career. You can earn and purchase commemorative cosmetic items and an exclusive skin themed after the Beacon of Hope himself in celebration of this moment. Also available are the Risen Legend, Immortalized Legend, and Signature Immortalized Legend Collections, featuring Tristana skins co-developed with Caps himself.

Experience the fearless blend of creativity, adaptability, and unbridled enthusiasm that characterizes Caps' career in the Hall of Legends battle pass with 100 total levels of unlockable rewards, including commemorative skins, icons, and an exclusive callback honoring an iconic Caps champion. Reward highlights include:

  • Risen Legend Orianna Skin & Border
  • Risen Legend Orianna Event Chroma
  • Freljord Taliyah, Elderwood LeBlanc, Empyrean Akali Skins
  • 125 Mythic Essence
  • 11 Orbs
  • 15 Caps-Themed Icons & Emotes
  • Unkillable Demon Cactus Ward
  • Beacon of Hope Banner
  • "Martin 1" Title
  • And more!

    • Champions

    Bard

    Bard has been a meta staple for much of the year. Earlier we toned his damage down to what we think are reasonable levels, so this time we are going to target his durability which has also stood out as high given his mobility and long range ultimate utility.

    Base Stats

  • Armor: 34 + 5/Level ⇒ 32 + 4.7/Level

    • Cassiopeia

    Cassio has always scaled with skill, but this year has propelled her to new heights of pro play dominance despite being weaker for average players. These adjustments should tap down her laning power, especially in pro where defensive purchases are valued more than raw AP, while giving her back some scaling power. It will still be critical to use empowered E's, but raising her floor lets us be a bit more flexible with tuning.

    Passive - Serpentine Grace

  • Move Speed Bonus: 6% - 40% (based on level) ⇒ 5% - 36% (based on level)

    • Q - Noxious Blast

  • Damage: 75 / 110 / 145 / 180 / 215 ⇒ 65 / 100 / 135 / 170 / 205
  • Ability Power Ratio: 65% ⇒ 75%

    • E - Twin Fang

  • Mana Cost: 40 ⇒ 45
  • Base Ability Power Ratio: 10% ⇒ 20%
  • Enhanced Ability Power Ratio: 55% ⇒ 45%
  • Total Ability Power Ratio: 65% ⇒ 65%
  • Damage: 52 - 120 ⇒ 50 - 120

    • R - Petrifying Gaze

  • Damage: 150 / 250 / 350 ⇒ 125 / 225 / 325
  • Ability Power Ratio: 50% ⇒ 75%

    • Ekko

    As one of our assassins that offer opponents a wider mix of gameplay options, Ekko has found a slightly weak steady state since Dusk & Dawn's update mid year. We believe he has some room for power, especially in mid where he scales slightly worse, without buffing his Hail of Blades pattern.

    Q - Timewinder

  • Mana Cost: 50 / 60 / 70 / 80 / 90 ⇒ 40 / 50 / 60 / 70 / 80
  • Return Damage Ability Power Ratio: 60% ⇒ 70%

    • Kassadin

    Kassadin had a strong start to 2026 but hasn't regained his…footing…since our earlier nerfs. His Q should feel more punchy with his scaling, and we're aiming to provide more early agency through good Riftwalk usage without touching his late game fantasy.

    Q - Null Sphere

  • Ability Power Ratio: 70% AP ⇒ 80% AP

    • R - Riftwalk

  • Base Damage: 70 / 90 / 110 ⇒ 80 / 95 / 110

    • Master Yi

    Yi drew the short end of the stick on the Rageblade bugfix from earlier this year due to his double strike interactions. While the actual impact for most Rageblade users was minor (and we are compensating Rageblade as well for that this patch), he was impacted harder than the other users. He's also just been unable to scale as well as a melee carry compared to his normal power level, so we are also giving him a buff up.

    Base Stats

  • Armor Growth: 33 + 4.5/Level ⇒ 33 + 5/Level

    • R - Highlander

  • Move Speed: 35 / 45 / 55% ⇒ 40 / 50 / 60%

    • Nautilus

    Nautilus has been sitting near the top of the meta for the entire year, even before our work to bring other tank supports up in power, and we feel nerfing him will open up room for a more variety. That said, we know a lot of his value is in being able to lock down champions effectively, and that'll remain a core strength.

    Base Stats

  • Attack Damage: 61 + 3.3/Level ⇒ 58 + 3.3/Level

    • Q - Dredge Line

  • Damage: 85 / 130 / 175 / 220 / 265 (+90% AP) ⇒ 85 / 125 / 165 / 205 / 245 (+90% AP)

    • Seraphine

    Seraphine bot has been a source of frustration for opponents for some time, despite a minor nerf a few patches ago. We are nerfing her E's rank up to target this head on, as support Seraphine usually maxes it last (which basically means she never has it maxed as a support.)

    E - Beat Drop

  • Cooldown: 11 / 10.5 / 10 / 9.5 / 9s ⇒ 11s

    • Syndra

    Our MSI changes were effective at pulling her to the forefront of pro play for the first time in years, but unfortunately she's too performant in specific solo queue settings. Our data shows that W damage is a meaningfully larger share of damage in the tiers where she's stronger than desired, so this should help tap her down while still preserving her core fantasies. Her passive is also now better breakpointed to increase reliance on Lost Chapter in early-mid levels, nerfing her higher winrate builds that make do with less mana investment.

    Passive - Transcendent

  • Splinter Mana: 20 - 255 ⇒ 20 - 199

    • W - Force of Will

  • Cooldown: 12 / 11 / 10 / 9 / 8s ⇒ 13 / 12 / 11 / 10 / 9s

    • Viego

    Viego's winrate has been on a downward trend recently, and his players have noticed and begun dropping him. He has a fair bit of room to bring up, both just generally and for the viability of his more bruisery alt build.

    Base Stats

  • Attack Damage Growth: 3.5 ⇒ 4

    • Passive - Sovereign's Domination

  • Heal: 2% (+…. ) ⇒ 2% (+ 2.5% per 100 bonus AD) (+ 2% per 100 AP) (+ 5% per 100% bonus attack speed) (+ 2% per 500 bonus HP) of the target's maximum health

    •  

    Zaahen

    We're using a QoL change here as an opportunity to give Zaahen some love! This might read as a nerf, but Zaahen's Q lined up with his passive in such a way that it meant he always left his resurrection (and GA, Zilean R) with Q on CD, so now he's always happier. His Q2 is also a clean double of his Q1 base damage now.

     

    Q - The Darkin Glaive

  •   NEW   Cooldown Behavior: If Q is active, it is now placed on Cooldown immediately upon being put in Resurrection
  • Q2 Damage: 25 / 50 / 75 / 100 / 125 (+20 / 25 / 30 / 35 / 40% bonus AD) ⇒ 30 / 60 / 90 / 120 / 150 (+20 / 25 / 30 / 35 / 40% bonus AD)

    • Zeri

    Zeri has been slowly climbing in winrate with the recent Runaan's Hurricane and Yun Tal Wildarrows buffs. She now sits very high in winrate compared to her historical resting, which is worrying for a champ that is so skill intensive. As she has also begun showing up in pro, we expect she has a high chance of becoming meta dominant, so we are pulling some power out of her burst and waveclear.

    W - Ultrashock Laser

  • Damage: 30 / 70 / 110 / 150 / 190 (+120% tAD) ⇒ 30 / 70 / 110 / 150 / 190 (+100% tAD)
  • Wall Damage: 45 / 105 / 165 / 225 / 285 (+180% tAD) ⇒ 45 / 105 / 165 / 225 / 285 (+150% tAD)
  • Critical Strike: 150% (+15% IE)

    • Items

    Guinsoo's Rageblade

    In light of the bugfix nerfing rageblade by a minor amount by pushing back when the first double hit triggers, we are compensating with a similarly minor QoL buff to help players get it stacked up and keep it stacked.

  • Seething Strike Stack Duration: 3s ⇒ 4s

    • Classic

    Our third League Classic patch has our biggest content drop to date: Five brand new old champions! Do you want to remove as much gameplay as possible with Poppy's Diplomatic Immunity? Untargetably Blade Waltz the entire enemy team as Fiora? Deliver taunt explosions as Galio? Experience the fabled early Xin Zhao kit (he's been nerfed, don't worry)? Shyvana's also here.

    We've got a smaller balance patch than before, as we're in a much better state balance-wise. Some of our bugfixes had substantial winrate impact, so we're returning some power we took away in a few cases. Otherwise, we're just addressing the game's biggest outliers.

    Champions

      NEW   Fiora

    Welcome back Classic Fiora, who existed from 2012-2015. Fiora is a deadly duelist, poised to deal tons of damage to isolated targets while also excelling in short trades by Riposting their strikes back at them. You'll probably want a Ravenous Hydra to have access to wave clear. Some things never change.

    Passive - Duelist

  • Fiora regenerates health whenever she damages enemies. This regeneration can stack when hitting champions.


    • Q - Lunge

  • Fiora dashes to strike a nearby enemy. Lunge can be cast a second time at no additional cost..


    • W - Riposte

  • Passive: Fiora gain bonus Attack Damage
  • Active: Fiora parries the next attack within a short time, dealing damage back to her attacker.


    • E - Burst of Speed

  • Fiora gains Attack Speed for a few seconds. Attacks and Lunges during this time grant her a stacking Move Speed bonus.


    • R - Blade Waltz

  • This is why you're really here. Fiora becomes untargetable and dashes around the battlefield, striking nearby enemies for (say it with me) tons of damage. All strikes apply on-hit effects and repeated hits on the same target deal reduced damage.

    •   NEW   Galio

    Classic Galio existed from 2010-2017 and was one part mage, one part AP bruiser, one part tank, one part support. He still wants to build Magic Resist to scale his offense, but almost everything about him is different from the modern-day champion.

    Passive - Runic Skin

  • Galio gains a portion of his Magic Resist as Ability Power. Hooray for one-sentence passives!


    • Q - Resolute Smite

  • Galio fires a concussive blast from his eyes that damages and slows enemies where it lands.


    • W - Bulwark

  • Galio gives a nearby allied champion bonus Armor and Magic Resist. While buffed, whenever they take damage, Galio is healed.


    • E - Righteous Gust

  • Galio unleashes a gust of wind that damages enemies in a line and leaves behind a directional draft, which gives all allies movement speed as long as they're moving with the current.
  • Hwei stole this ability. What a jerk.


    • R - Idol of Durand

  • Galio channels to taunt all nearby enemies, taking reduced damage in the process. After channeling, Galio damages all enemies caught in the area, increasing based on how many times he was hit while channeling.

    •   NEW   Poppy

    Do you think League of Legends has too much gameplay? Do you want your opponents to literally have no counterplay to you? No damage, no CC, nothing? We have the Demacian for you. Initially available from 2010-2015, Classic Poppy is a single-target terror with the option to become completely immune to all enemies but one.

    Passive - Valiant Fighter

  • All damage to Poppy beyond 10% of her current health is reduced by 50%
  • Just in case you thought she was too easy to kill already


    • Q - Devastating Blow

  • Poppy's next attack deals bonus damage based on her target's max HP


    • W - Paragon of Demacia

  • Passive: Poppy gains Armor and Attack Damage (up to a cap) whenever she deals or takes Attacks herself.
  • Active: Immediately gain max stacks of Paragon of Demacia and gain increased Move Speed for several seconds


    • E - Heroic Charge

  • Poppy charges at an enemy, damaging and knocking this back. If they collide with a wall, they take more damage and are stunned.


    • R - Diplomatic Immunity

  • Poppy picks an enemy. For the next few seconds no one else can do anything to her and she deals bonus damage to them.
  • Don't be fooled by the bonus damage. Ult Soraka and then kill the enemy ADC. There's no counter-play.
  • I can't believe they got rid of this spell during her rework.

    •   NEW   Shyvana

    We chose 2011-2013 for Classic Shyvana, so this is a true blast from the past. Our biggest pro tip for you is Frozen Mallet. If they're slowed, they can't run away.

    Passive - Fury of the Dragonborn

  • Shyvana's basic attacks enhance each of her basic abilities. They reduce Q's cooldown, increase W's duration, deal a fraction of E's initial damage, and generate Fury for her ultimate.


    • Q - Twin Bite

  • Shyvana's next attack strikes her target twice, dealing bonus damage.
  • In dragon form, Twin Bite deals damage in a cone in front of her.


    • W - Burnout

  • Shyvana gains Move Speed and continually damages enemies around her.
  • In dragon form, Burnout leaves a trail of fire that damages enemies who stand on it.


    • E - Flame Breath

  • Shyvana unleashes a fireball that damages the first enemy hit and reduces their armor
  • In dragon form, she unleashes a cone of fireballs, hitting more enemies.


    • R - Dragon's Descent

  • Passive: Shyvana gains bonus Armor and Magic Resist. This bonus is doubled while in dragon form.
  • Shyvana transforms into a dragon, flying forward to damage and knock back all enemies encountered during her flight.

    •   NEW   Xin Zhao

    Classic Xin Zhao takes on his kit from 2012-2017. If you're looking for some straightforward right click until they're dead gameplay, look no further!

    Passive - Challenge

  • Xin Zhao Challenges his most recent attack target, reducing their Armor.


    • Q - Three Talon Strike

  • Xin Zhao's next three basic attacks deal bonus damage and reduce his other cooldowns by 1 second. The third attack knocks up his target.


    • W - Battle Cry

  • Passive: Every third basic attack heals Xin Zhao.
  • Active: Xin Zhao gains bonus Attack Speed for several seconds.


    • E - Audacious Charge

  • Xin Zhao dashes an enemy, Challenging them. Nearby enemies, including the target, take damage and are slowed.


    • R - Crescent Sweep

  • Xin Zhao sweeps all enemies around him, dealing damage and gaining Armor and Magic Resist for each enemy struck. Every enemy except his Challenge target are knocked back.

    • Anivia

    Anivia is our single top performer in mid lane, so she's been slated for nerfs. We've got several changes this patch, all of which are re-tuning her numbers back to 2013 accuracy.

    Q - Flash Frost

  • Missile Speed: 950 ⇒ 850
  • Manual Detonation Stun Duration: 1s ⇒ 0.75s
  • Manual Detonation Radius: 230 ⇒ 210
  • Minimum Delay for Recast: 0 ⇒ 0.25s

    • Gangplank

    Gangplank is performing worst of all conventional top laners and is deserving of a large buff. As with many of our changes on Classic, we're reverting old nerfs from 2011 and 2012. We're playing up his dreams of being a banker and sharing the wealth when it's time to go all in.

    Q - Parrrley

  • Bonus Gold on Kill: 4 / 5 / 6 / 7 / 8 ⇒ 4 / 6 / 8 / 10 / 12


    • E - Raise Morale

  • Active Attack Damage: 12 / 19 / 26 / 33 / 40 ⇒ 14 / 22 / 30 / 38 / 46
  • Active Move Speed: 8 / 11 / 14 / 17 / 20% ⇒ 10 / 14 / 18 / 22 / 26%
  • Ally Bonus: Allies still gain 50% of Gangplank's bonuses

    • Heimerdinger

    Heimerdinger's bugfix last patch ended up being a massive hit to his power, well above what we expected. So we're buffing him back up, partially reverting some of our previous nerfs. Because the double damage turret bugfix was significantly top lane skewed, we're looking to buff his performance in top lane most of all and fix a couple of minor mismatches that escaped his release.

    Base Stats

  • Base Health Regeneration: 4.5 ⇒ 5.05


    • Q - H-28G Evolution Turret

  • Base Damage: 28 / 36 / 44 / 52 / 60 ⇒ 30 / 38 / 46 / 54 / 62


    • W - Hextech Micro-Rockets

  • Mana Cost: 65 / 85 / 105 / 125 / 145 ⇒ 60 / 75 / 90 / 105 / 120


    • E - CH-1 Concussion Grenade

  • Cooldown: 14 / 13 / 12 / 11 / 10s ⇒ 13 / 12 / 11 / 10 / 9s
  • Cast Range: 920 ⇒ 925

    • Kayle

    Kayle isn't performing too well in her most popular role of top lane, so we're here to lend her a wing. We've got a large change to her passive, which is a boost of functionally 17-32 ability power. All in all, this should result in a Kayle with more damage, more healing, more everything.

    Passive - Holy Fervor

  • Ability Power Gained: 30% bonus AD ⇒ 30% total AD

    • Malzahar

    Malzahar is one of our best-performing mid laners, primarily as an AP threat, and is due for a small nerf. We completed a pass of minor differences from his 2013 form and have some changes to Voidlings as a result, which should skew toward making AD Malzahar better without affecting AP Malzahar much. Continuing on the trend of AD Malzahar, we're raising his overall attack speed, so that he can use those potential AD items better. Meanwhile, on the AP nerf front, we have a meaningful bugfix to R, which will reduce its damage in several circumstances, plus an AP ratio nerf to bring him in line.

    Base Stats

  • Attack Speed Growth: 1.36% ⇒ 3%
  • Attack Speed Ratio: 0.625 ⇒ 0.658


    • Passive - Summon Voidling

  • Movement Speed: 400 ⇒ 460
  • Attack Cast Frame: 12 ⇒ 9
  • Gold on Kill: 2 ⇒ 12


    • Q - Call of the Void

  • Ability Power Ratio: 80% ⇒ 70%


    • R - Nether Grasp

  • Bugfix: R no longer continues to deal damage if the channel stops.

    • Nasus

    Nasus is the top dog of top lane and it's by a lot. Thankfully, we've got some substantial bugfixes that should put his bark and his bite on more equal footing. First, we're fixing a bug where his Q stacks could crit, which means for all you Trinity Force enjoyers, that's a big hit to Q damage about 10% of the time. For Wither, there are two bugs worth noting and a single change for period-accuracy. The slow now updates every 1 second (affected by tenacity) instead of every 0.5 seconds, unaffected. So now Tenacity won't cut off the top-end of his slow. However, it was also bugged to use the per-second update every 0.5 seconds, meaning the maximum slow was much higher than it should have been. Fixing both bugs should net out to an appropriate nerf for the ability.

    Q - Siphoning Strike

  • Bonus Damage from stacks can no longer critically strike


    • W - Wither

  • Slow ramps every: 0.5s ⇒ 1.0s, affected by Tenacity
  • Bugfix: The slow no longer ramps up twice as hard as it should

    • Warwick

    Warwick is the top dog of the jungle and it's by a lot. With Feral Flare's build path turning back into attack speed, Warwick's doing even better than he ever has. Accordingly, we're pulling back even further on how much auto-attack power he gets, mostly from historic changes in his past. We're also pulling in part of a nerf from 4.21. He was a real terror back in the patch before then...

    Base Stats

  • Attack Speed: 0.644 ⇒ 0.625


    • Passive - Eternal Thirst

  • Base Damage: 3 - 16, linear scaling ⇒ 3 + 0.5 per level until level 9, then +1 per level


    • W - Hunter's Call

  • Cooldown: 24 / 22 / 20 / 18 / 16s ⇒ 30 / 27 / 24 / 21 / 18s


    • R - Infinite Duress

  • Damage: 250 / 335 / 420 + 200% bonus AD ⇒ 180 / 300 / 420 + 200% bonus AD
  • Cast Indicator: Updated the cast indicator to better reflect its cast range

    • Council - Poll 1 Results

    Thank you, Summoners, for casting your votes in the inaugural Council! We aggregated the results from across the world and you can read them below. The questions with actionable results will be released in an upcoming patch, specifically:

  • Reviving all 3 proposed items.
  • Adding modern jungle timers.
  • Turtle, Duck.

    • How does game length feel?

  • 1. Way too short - 1.87%
  • 2. Too short - 5.88%
  • 3. About right - 52.80%
  • 4. Too long - 26.21%
  • 5. Way too long - 13.24%

    • When is a game too long?

  • 1. 30 minutes - 16.75%
  • 2. 40 minutes - 32.68%
  • 3. 50 minutes - 29.29%
  • 4. 60 minutes - 11.64%
  • 5. No preferred maximum - 9.63%

    • Which of these items do you want us to revive in Classic? Each item that scores higher than 50% is added, including "All 3."

  • 1. Zz'Rot Portal - 16.16%
  • 2. Cloak and Dagger - 3.75%
  • 3. Moonflair Spellblade - 5.11%
  • 4. All 3 - 60.67%
  • 5. None - 14.32%

    • Should Classic add jungle timers? If options 1 and 2 receive more than 50% combined, the higher of those two options wins.

  • 1. Yes – Add modern jungle timers that are always visible on the minimap - 45.74%
  • 2. Yes – Only when the scoreboard is open - 23.46%
  • 3. No – Keep the current minimap - 30.79%

    • Base gates were added at the start of Season 5 to give the defending team a way to protect its base without relying on more extreme comeback mechanics. Should we keep base gates in the game?

  • 1. Yes - 55.03%
  • 2. No - 44.97%

    • How snowbally do games feel to you now?

  • 1. Significantly too snowbally - 8.89%
  • 2. Slightly too snowbally - 24.99%
  • 3. About right - 48.82%
  • 4. Slightly not snowbally enough - 12.24%
  • 5. Significantly not snowbally enough - 5.06%

    • Do you feel that the ward trinkets improve Classic gameplay?

  • 1. Yes, I like them - 69.72%
  • 2. No, I don't like them - 30.28%

    • We're adding 2 critters to the river, 1 at top and 1 at bottom. What should the critter pairings be (top first, bottom second)?

  • 1. Turtle, Turtle - 11.31%
  • 2. Turtle, Duck- 52.09%
  • 3. Duck, Turtle - 28.39%
  • 4. Duck, Duck - 8.21%

    • Systems

    We've made some changes around Classic Skin Chromas and their distribution. Instead of directly selling Classic Skin Chromas, we're unifying this product with their associated Base Skin. We're hoping this simplifies things and removes some edge cases (where players could effectively pay double if they purchased the Classic Chroma and then the Base Skin).

    For those players who have only purchased the Classic Chroma, we'll be granting the associated Base Skin for free!

    Baron Rammus will be going into the vault in 26.20. You can acquire him at a discounted price until then!"

    Bugfixes

  • Fixed a bug where Teemo's traps did not last the appropriate 10 minutes.
  • Fixed a bug where Akali's Q cast indicator did not accurately reflect its cast range.
  • Fixed a bug where Akali's W could be cast while moving.
  • Fixed a bug where Akali's R cast indicator did not accurately reflect its cast range.
  • Fixed a bug where Skarner's E could heal for less than the full amount.
  • Fixed a bug where Nidalee's Cougar E hit range was 310 instead of 350.
  • Fixed a bug where Nidalee's Human E cast range was 900 instead of 600.

    • ARAM: Mayhem

    Hello Mayhemers! In this patch, we're making more behind-the-scenes adjustments to Augment offerings.

    We've heard your feedback around some Augments showing up on champions that don't make sense on them, such as AP-focused Augments on Vayne.

    We're taking another pass at these cases and will continue improving the Augment pools to provide more relevant and exciting choices for each champion.

    For bugfixes, we've also addressed a few unintended interactions with Ultra Hydra and Ravenous Hydra that could be abused for some…questionable results.

    Thanks for the feedback, and see you on the Bridge!

    Augments

    Clown College

  •   NEW   Status: Re-enabled

    • Bugfixes

  • Fixed a bug where item damage triggers the cleave effect when you have Upgrade Ravenous Hydra.
  • Fixed a bug where En Passant fail to function when two or more players have it on the same team.
  • Fixed a bug where Viego can get multiple Tiamat when possessing others while having Ultra Hydra.
  • Fixed a bug where extra gold can be gained by selling and re-purchasing a Hydra item with Ultra Hydra augment equipped.
  • Fixed a bug where players can purchase multiple Ravenous Hydra and gain Upgrade Ravenous Hydra lifesteal on all three when paired with Quest: Ultra Hydra.
  • Fixed a bug where Clown College's Deceive dealt incorrect damage with critical strike ratio.
  • Fixed a bug where Rite of Ascension may seal enhanced abilities.

    • Bugfixes & QoL Changes

  • Fixed a bug where Baron Nashor's max stacks of Void Corruption was higher than intended.
  • Fixed a bug where Serpent's Fang's Shield Reaver damage applied Omnivamp.
  • Fixed a bug where Diana's R VFX may not play properly around different areas of the map.
  • Fixed a bug where Viego possessing Kled could result in an infinite looping sound effect.

html:
We're soon coming up on the Worlds patch (which is the patch after this one), so our first round of pro-focused Summoner's Rift changes are coming up here. We've identified some potential fringe picks for the tournament that could also provide some normal play variety without becoming disruptive with a nudge up in power, and knocking some individual meta outliers as well (and also Nasus). Systemically, the top lane role quest has been quite successful at freeing up top laners to skip Teleport, so we think increasing their map influence through that spell (both if you take it from the start of game or just through the quest) is a fair place to give the role some power.

Looking for more information on all things League of Legends? Check out our community-run wiki here!

Wrong patch notes? You can find the TFT patch notes here!

Patch Highlights

Coven Janna, Coven Mel, Old God Anivia, Old God Urgot will be available September 23, 2026.

Team Voice

First up, we wanted to share an update on the rollout of Team Voice, which is our planned expansion to the existing pre-made party voice chat allowing you to chat with everyone on your team. While we originally announced this as coming to North America and Oceania in Patch 26.20, after extensive testing, we've made the call to postpone this a bit to make sure we're hitting the quality bar you deserve for the experience. We don't have a target patch just yet, but we're prioritizing ironing out the kinks as efficiently as we can, since we know this is a long awaited feature we need to get right.

Champions

Aatrox

We think The Darkin Blade has lost a fair bit of power with Sundered Sky nerfs that were aimed more at opening up the jungle meta, so we are giving him a bump so he remains a world-ending threat.

W - Infernal Chains

  • Cooldown: 20 / 18 / 16 / 14 / 12 seconds ⇒ 18 / 16.5 / 15 / 13.5 / 12 seconds

    • E - Umbral Dash

  • Health Heal Ratio: 1.1% per 100 bonus health ⇒ 1.3% per 100 bonus health

    • Aphelios

    Aphelios has been kiting the spotlight for a while now, even though he's a hypercarry in an enchanter meta that should favor him, so we're looking to give him a little boost to encourage him to get out of his comfort zone.

    Calibrum

  • Moonshot Damage: 70 - 160 (+42 - 60% bonus AD) (+100% AP) ⇒ 80 - 170 (+42 - 60% bonus AD) (+100% AP)

    • Severum

  • Healing: 2 - 7.1%, increased to 5 - 17.75% ⇒ 2 - 8%, increased to 5 - 20%

    • Gravitum

  • Slow: 30% for 2.5 seconds, decaying to 10% after 0.7 seconds ⇒ 30% for 2.5 seconds, decaying to 15% after 0.7 seconds

    • Infernum

  • Duskwave Cooldown: 9 / 8.25 / 7.5 / 6.75 / 6 seconds ⇒ 8 / 7.25 / 6.5 / 5.75 / 5 seconds

    • Crescendum

  • Mini-Crescendum Damage: 15% AD, decreasing by 1.5% AD to a minimum of 5% AD for the 8th+ chakram ⇒ 16% AD, decreasing by 1.5% AD to a minimum of 5% AD for the 9th+ chakram

    • Aurora

    Despite not receiving any changes since last year, Aurora has fallen off as we've had to nerf Rocketbelt into a fairer state. We're giving our favorite Bryni a bit more power in her waveclear and outplay potential with her ultimate.

    E - The Weirding

  • Base Damage: 70 / 110 / 150 / 190 / 230 ⇒ 80 / 120 / 160 / 200 / 240

    • R - Between Worlds

  • Rift Duration: 1.75 / 2.5 / 3.25 seconds ⇒ 2.25 / 2.75 / 3.25 seconds

    • Draven

    Since all bot laners received significantly increased gold income thanks to role quests, Draven's potential to gain a gold advantage through his Adoration stacks has lost some of its impact. We're giving him a helping hand (axe?) by tapping up his early game damage.

    Base Stats

  • Attack Damage: 62 ⇒ 64

    • Elise

    This year started strong for AP junglers that could use Dusk and Dawn, but others like Elise have been in a weak spot for a while, so we are helping out our friendly neighborhood spider with clear speed and damage.

    Passive - Spider Queen

  • Passive Magic Damage On-Hit: 12 / 22 / 32 / 42 ⇒ 14 / 24 / 34 / 44

    • W - Skittering Frenzy

  • Bonus Attack Speed: 60 / 75 / 90 / 105 / 120% ⇒ 70 / 85 / 100 / 115 / 130%

    • Fiora

    Our Grand Duelist has room to shine a bit more when she succeeds after finding her opening, without giving her sharper 1v1 tools.

    Base Stats

  • Health Growth: 99 ⇒ 105

    • R - Grand Challenge

  • Heal Range: 550 ⇒ 600
  • Heal Per Tick: 18.75 / 25 / 31.25 (+15% bonus AD) ⇒ 20 / 26.25 / 32.5 (+17.5% bonus AD)
  • Maximum Heal: 375 / 500 / 625 (+300% bonus AD) ⇒ 400 / 525 / 650 (+350% bonus AD)

    • Kha'Zix

    Kha'Zix has been on the fringe of the meta now that the jungle is no longer dominated by Sundered Sky users. We are taking this opportunity to buff some of his weaker evolves to give him the flexibility to adapt and overcome.

    Passive - Unseen Threat

  • Damage: 17 - 136 (+50% bonus AD) ⇒ 22 - 141 (+50% bonus AD)

    • W - Void Spike

  • Evolved Slow Duration: 2 seconds ⇒ 2.25 seconds

    • E - Leap

  • Evolved Range Bonus: +200 ⇒ +300

    • Lillia

    Lillia is on the edge of being viable at higher levels of play and we believe her current pattern requires her to get in danger's way, so we're helping her durability. We also want to give Lillia opportunities to really be a playmaker so we're making the enemies she lullabies a little extra sleepy.

    Base Stats

  • Armor: 22 ⇒ 24

    • R - Lilting Lullaby

  • Sleep Duration: 2 seconds ⇒ 2.5 seconds

    • Lucian

    Years ago, we added the Vigilance Passive so Lucian bot players didn't feel like their champ was being nerfed because of mid laners, which ended up being super effective. We think now is a good opportunity to adjust the tuning of the passive and strike a balance between both roles.

    Passive - Vigilance

  • Empowered On-Hit Damage: 15 (+20% AD) ⇒ 5 (+15% AD)

    • Q - Piercing Light

  • Base Damage: 80 / 115 / 150 / 185 / 220 (+100% bonus AD) ⇒ 90 / 130 / 170 / 210 / 250 (+100% bonus AD)

    • Master Yi

    Somewhat overdue, but because Duskblade was removed a while ago, we're removing the Ability Haste penalty we had to apply to his Q CDR mechanic. This should have minimal impact on Summoner's Rift, but we see you Mayhem and Arena!

    Q - Alpha Strike

  • Cooldown Refund on Hit: -1 second, scaling down with Ability Haste ⇒ 1 second

    • Nasus

    Nasus is difficult to keep down these days, and part of that is how quickly getting his early stacks leads to more reliable stacking. These higher highs will be compensated with some lower lows through some more vulnerability early on with lower damage and lifesteal lane sustain values off of that, and a bit longer before he really comes online.

    Q - Siphoning Strike

  • Bonus Damage: 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 / 120 ⇒ 30 / 50 / 70 / 90 / 110

    • Nocturne

    Nocturne has been a popular and powerful jungler in both pro and solo-queue for a while, so we're hitting the map presence and dueling power he benefits from through his ultimate.

    R - Paranoia

  • Cooldown: 140 / 115 / 90 seconds ⇒ 160 / 130 / 100 seconds

    • Poppy

    Poppy's flex potential and jungle presence has been a bit problematic, suppressing many champions across the board as a strong counterpick. For this change, we're targeting her flexibility by reverting a previous buff to jungle clear.

    Q - Hammer Shock

  • Minion/Monster Maximum Health Cap: 85 / 120 / 155 / 190 / 225 ⇒ 70 / 105 / 140 / 175 / 210

    • Rumble

    At higher levels of play, we've seen Rumble continue to take over games, even after our changes earlier this year designed to hit his power in lane. Here, we're making some modifications to his passive that's much more elite-skewed, while giving Rumble in the Jungle some compensation.

    Passive - Junkyard Titan

  • Overheat Attack Speed: 50 - 130% ⇒ 30 - 100%
  • Monster Cap: 65 - 150 ⇒ 90 - 175

    • Ryze

    Between strong itemization options and best-in-class skirmish and roam potential demonstrated by his most skilled players, it's high time we put some restraints on the archmage, while giving him some help with bad solo queue matchups.

    Base Stats

  • Armor Growth: 4.2 ⇒ 4.7

    • Q - Overload

  • Flux Bonus Damage: 25 / 50 / 75 / 100% increased damage ⇒ 15 / 40 / 65 / 90% increased damage

    • E - Spell Flux

  • Mana Cost: 35 / 45 / 55 / 65 / 75 ⇒ 40 / 50 / 60 / 70 / 80

    • Vi

    Vi has been a meta staple for the entire year, and now that Sundered Sky is in a better spot, we're going after her durability and early clear speed to make her a riskier pick who can still bring the pain if you are willing to build for it.

    Base Stats
