Bee wee woop - it's time for WORLDS! For Summoner's Rift, this is the patch we'll be seeing our year-defining competitive play on. Lock in, because we've got some adjustments to some pro staples like Ambessa & K'Sante, and buffs to weaker champions who might be on the edge of viability like Kennen & Kindred. Rocketbelt is getting another tap to make it a bit worse at just being a purchasable Flash for immobile characters, with some immediate compensation for some core users because this is the patch and it's the only shot we've got. There's quite a bit more, including fun stuff for Mayhem & Classic, so read on for details!

Looking for more information on all things League of Legends? Check out our community-run wiki here!

Wrong patch notes? You can find the TFT patch notes here!

Champions

Ambessa

Ambessa has been too reliable in her late game output for players with high mastery in all brackets, but especially pro-play.

Passive - Drakehound's Step

  • Damage: 5 - 30 (+25% bonus AD) ⇒ 5 - 25 (+20% bonus AD)

    • Ashe

    Ashe is one of the premier marksmen in pro play at the moment, and we're seeing her output too much raw damage given her position as the highest utility marksman in the game.

    Base Stats

  • Attack Damage per Level: 3.5 ⇒ 3

    • Cassiopeia

    Our changes two patches ago to Cassiopeia have been pretty good directionally, with most players being proportionally less impacted from those adjustments than pros. We're taking another swing at her early resources because of how dominant she still is in early laning, making her work a little harder to create an advantage.

    Base Stats

  • Base Health: 630 ⇒ 610
  • Base Mana: 480 ⇒ 450

    • Diana

    While Diana's assassin build shines, her bruiser builds tend to be lagging a good bit behind. We want to inject a bit more power into that playstyle.

    W - Pale Cascade

  • Shield Bonus Health Ratio: 11% ⇒ 14%

    • Kennen

    Stacking the odds a bit more in his favor with his signature spell (in Riftbound) and offsetting Rocketbelt changes that he'll be a bit less excited about.

    E - Lightning Rush

  • Bonus Attack Speed: 40 / 50 / 60 / 70 / 80% ⇒ 50 / 60 / 70 / 80 / 90%

    • Kindred

    Kindred is currently a bit weak, so we're giving them buffs in areas that won't make them much more overwhelming in early invades. Optimistically, they'd also make a pretty unique addition to the meta.

    W - Wolf's Frenzy

  • Monster Mod: 150% ⇒ 165%

    • E - Mounting Dread

  • Slow Duration: 1s ⇒ 1.5s
  • Small Monster Targeting: Enabled ⇒ Removed

    • K'Sante

    Warding off this warden from being as reliable as a blind pick in coordinated play - hurting early mana and consistent W damage reduction, which should be skewed for elite audiences.

    W - Path Maker

  • Mana Cost: 40 / 45 / 50 / 55 / 60 ⇒ 45 / 50 / 55 / 60 / 65
  • W Base/All-Out Damage Reduction: 30 / 75% ⇒ 25 / 70%

    • Lillia

    Last patch we looked to inject a bit more power into the deer, but didn't quite see the movement we were looking for. We believe there is a bit more room for her to really prance around various levels of play so we are following up with another buff that'll really help her shine.

    R - Lilting Lullaby

  • Duration: 2.5s ⇒ 2.5 / 2.75 / 3s

    • Lucian

    Last patch's adjustment to help normalize mid and bot performance ended up landing as a nerf for bot lane, so we're following up with a buff to make up for the lost power.

    Base Stats

  • Attack Damage: 60 + 2.5/Level ⇒ 60 + 2.9/Level

    • Mordekaiser

    Windows between Mordekaiser's ultimates make it hard to keep up with the pace of much of his opposition. His bread and butter (Q) can also feel less impactful as the pace of the game increases, so we think it can do more damage later on.

    Q - Obliterate

  • Scaling Level 10-20: (+5/lvl) ⇒ (+7/lvl)

    • R - Realm of Death

  • Cooldown: 140 / 120 / 100s ⇒ 120 / 110 / 100s

    • Neeko

    Rocketbelt's adjustment this patch will probably land as a small nerf for Neeko, so we're giving her some minor compensation

    E - Tangle-Barbs

  • Base Damage: 70 / 105 / 140 / 175 / 210 (+65% AP) ⇒ 80 / 115 / 150 / 185 / 220 (+65% AP)
  • Empowered Root Duration: 1.8 / 2.1 / 2.4 / 2.7 / 3s ⇒ 2 / 2.25 / 2.5 / 2.75 / 3s

    • Smolder

    Smolder has lost quite a bit of power over the last few patches, with the Cleaver ranged nerf and bot lane meta changes disfavoring him significantly. We're further encouraging crit builds to bring his bruiser and full crit builds closer in power.

    Passive - Dragon Practice

  • Super Scorcher Bonus Magic Damage: 25 - 55% (+0-9% with IE) of Dragon Practice Stacks, scaling with Crit Chance ⇒ 25 - 60% (+0-10.5% with IE) of Dragon Practice Stacks, scaling with Crit Chance
  • Flap Flap Flap Bonus Magic Damage: 8 - 12.8% (+0-1.44% with IE) of Dragon Practice Stacks, scaling with Crit Chance ⇒ 8 - 14% (+0-1.8% with IE) of Dragon Practice Stacks, scaling with Crit Chance

    • R - Mmooommmm!

  • Self Heal: 100 / 135 / 170 (+50% bonus AD) (+75% AP) ⇒ 100 / 175 / 250 (+75% bonus AD) (+75% AP)

    • Swain

    We're giving Swain mid a moderate buff this patch while also making an adjustment that should help normalize his mid and bot lane performance.

    Base Stats

  • Base Magic Resistance: 31 ⇒ 34
  • Base Armor: 25 ⇒ 23

    • W - Vision of Empire

  • Damage: 70 / 105 / 140 / 175 / 210 (+60%) ⇒ 70 / 115 / 160 / 205 / 250 (+60%)
  • Cooldown: 22 / 21 / 20 / 19 / 18s ⇒ 20 / 19 / 18 / 17 / 16s

    • Tahm Kench

    As one of the tank supports with the lowest health regen, and many health scaling values on his abilities, Tahm Kench lost out on the recent adjustments to the support item. We're giving him compensation for that.

    Q - Tongue Lash

  • Base Healing: 10 / 13.75 / 17.5 / 21.25 / 25 ⇒ 10 / 20 / 30 / 40 / 50

    • Vayne

    Vayne has settled into a fairly weak spot, and while we still aren't totally happy with her top vs bot skew, we're getting closer. We're adjusting her base stats to help in bot where she needs to weather harass, and reverting a mana cost to her Q that simply felt way too bad.

    Base Stats

  • Health per 5: 4 + .5/Level ⇒ 5.5 +.4/Level

    • Q - Tumble

  • Mana Cost: 46 / 42 / 38 / 34 / 30 ⇒ 30

    • Yunara

    Yunara is the leading candidate for "handshake hyperscaler do nothing" and we want to avoid that becoming the dominant meta, especially heading into worlds.

    Q - Cultivation of Spirit

  • Passive On Hit Damage: 5 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 25 (+20% AP) ⇒ 3 / 8 / 13 / 18 / 23 (+20% AP)
  • Active On Hit Damage: 5 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 25 (+20% AP) ⇒ 3 / 8 / 13 / 18 / 23 (+20% AP)

    • W - Arc of Judgement

  • Slow Stacking: Stacks with other slows ⇒ No longer stacks with other slows

    • Items

    Experimental Hexplate

    We've been fairly unhappy with how this item has played out for ranged users, especially as a first rush in top lane where it makes them too resilient to burst and too lethal during all ins.

  • Ranged Mod: 70% of Value (35% Attack Speed, 14% Move Speed) ⇒ 50% of Value (25% Attack Speed, 10% Move Speed)

    • Hextech Rocketbelt

    Rocketbelt continues to be used a bit too much as an escape compared to a risky engage tool, so we are pulling back on its generic value in favor of emphasizing aggressive action with it, especially for AP Bruisers who rely on it for all ins.

  • Ability Haste: 20 ⇒ 10
  • Active Damage: 100 (+10% AP) ⇒ 135 (+15% AP)

    • Runaan's Hurricane

    This item was slightly overbuffed, so pulling back on that a bit.

  • Attack Damage per Bolt: 65% ⇒ 60%

    • Scoreboard Cleanup

    Our recent systemic buff-bar clarity work moved a lot of numbers from buffs onto items. These numbers began terrorizing your scoreboards (thanks, Death's Dance). The scoreboard should show strategically relevant information, not noisy in-the-moment combat state, and we're hiding most item numbers on the scoreboard to reflect this principle. Strategically relevant item numbers, like Tear of the Goddess items and Mejai's Soulstealer, remain on the scoreboard icons.

    The following items' icon counters are now hidden on the scoreboard:

  • Death's Dance
  • Haunting Guise
  • Liandry's Torment
  • Riftmaker
  • Kraken Slayer
  • Terminus
  • Guinsoo's Rageblade
  • Fiendhunter Bolts
  • Echoes of Helia
  • Dead Man's Plate
  • Spear of Shojin
  • Overlord's Bloodmail
  • Hullbreaker
  • Jak'sho the Protean
  • Force of Nature

    • Classic

    Are you ready for MORE new old champions?! Because we are! This time around we've got an eclectic crew who have no business forming a band together. Everyone please welcome Aatrox, Caitlyn, Irelia, Karma, and Quinn to the Fields of Justice.

    As a note, the Act II Battle Pass will be arriving with Patch 26.21

    Champions

      NEW   Aatrox

    Aatrox was just a baby, 3 patches old, when we chose to snapshot him for League Classic. He only ever had four balance changes before his rework in 2017 and subsequent rework in 2018, and we're excited to see how he'll perform again. He's an attack-focused fighter, damaging himself to gain attack speed and revive when he would be killed

  • Passive - Blood Well: Aatrox's basic abilities damage himself to fill his Blood Well, which gives him bonus attack speed. If he's killed, he empties his Blood Well to revive on the spot.
  • Q - Dark Flight: Aatrox flies up and crashes down, damaging and knocking up enemies in the area.
  • W - Blood Thirst / Blood Price: Toggle between Blood Thirst and Blood Price, each of which have bonus effects every three attacks. Blood Thirst heals Aatrox, increased when he's low on health. Blood Price deals bonus damage and self-damages.
  • E - Blades of Torment: Aatrox fires out two projectiles that damage and slow all enemies they touch.
  • R - Massacre: Aatrox damages all nearby enemy champions and gains bonus attack speed and attack range for several seconds.

    •   NEW   Caitlyn

    Classic's version of Caitlyn was live from 2011-2015. Did you know when she first came out, some players were upset that she was too similar to Miss Fortune?

  • Passive - Headshot: Every few attacks, Caitlyn fires a headshot, dealing bonus damage. Headshot charges up faster while attacking from brush.
  • Q - Piltover Peacemaker: Catilyn fires a piercing shot that deals less damage to each subsequent target.
  • W - Yordle Snap Trap: Caitlyn puts a trap on the ground that roots and damages the first enemy champion to walk over it. She can have up to 2 traps down at a time.
  • E - 90 Caliber Net: Caitlyn fires out a massive net, knocking herself back in the process. The net damages and slows the first enemy it hits.
  • R - Ace in the Hole: Caitlyn channels then fires a single bullet at an enemy champion, which deals tons of damage, but can be intercepted by other enemy champions.

    •   NEW   Irelia

    Welcome back the 2010-2018 version of Irelia! The original Trinity Force poster child is here to even the odds no matter how bad they look. She's been Q-max, W-max, and E-max at various points in time, so see what build order works for you! She's a fast but deceptively durable fighter who loves to be the underdog.

  • Passive - Ionian Fervor: Irelia gains bonus Tenacity based on how many visible enemy champions are nearby.
  • Q - Bladesurge: Irelia dashes to an enemy, dealing damage and applying on-hit effects. If it kills the target, Bladesurge's full cooldown and some of its mana cost are refunded.
  • W - Hiten Style: Passively, Irelia restores some health with every attack. While active, her attacks deal bonus true damage and restore even more health.
  • E - Equilibrium Strike: Irelia damages and slows a nearby enemy. If they have higher %HP than her, she stuns them instead..
  • R - Transcendent Blades: Irelia sequentially fires out four blades in a line, each damaging all enemies they hit and restoring some health to Irelia. This is definitely not just a wave clear tool.

    •   NEW   Karma

    Karma came out just two patches after Caitlyn and was only live for just over two years before being reworked in early 2013. Karma is arguably League's first battlemage, rewarding her for getting in the thick of it and making her stronger the more health she's missing.

  • Passive - Inner Flame: Karma gains bonus AP based on her missing health.
  • Q - Heavenly Wave: Karma fires out blades in a fan, err, cone in front of her, damaging all enemies it hits. If empowered with Mantra, it also heals all allies (herself included), scaling with their missing health.
  • W - Spirit Bond: Karma bonds with another target, giving allies (herself included) move speed, slowing enemies, and creating a tether between the two. Any champion caught in the clothesline is hasted or slowed as if they were the initial target. Enemies who get caught in the clothesline are damaged. If empowered with Mantra, all move speed effects are doubled.
  • E - Soul Shield: Karma shields a target. If empowered with Mantra, it also damages all enemies around her target.
  • R - Mantra: Mantra is available at level 1 and can hold up to two charges. She can cast it to empower her next basic ability.

    •   NEW   Quinn and Valor

    Quinn and Valor have returned, having only existed in this form for just over two years, from 2013-2015. Quinn is a ranged and evasive auto-attacker, while her ultimate calls in Valor to fight as a blistering-fast melee skirmisher instead.

  • Passive - Harrier: Valor periodically marks nearby enemies, whom Quinn can attack to deal bonus damage.
  • Q - Blinding Assault: Valor flies out to damage and blind enemies in an area.
  • W - Heightened Senses: Passively gives Quinn bonus attack and move speed whenever she triggers Harrier. Activate to briefly reveal a large area around her.
  • E - Vault: Quinn dashes to and then vaults off an enemy, damaging, knocking back, and slowing them. Valor then marks the target with Harrier.
  • R - Tag Team: Quinn retreats from the battlefield, sending Valor in her place. Valor has substantial bonus move speed, permanently has an empowered version of Heightened Senses' attack speed buff, and casts modified versions of Blinding Assault and Vault. Re-casting (R) casts Skystrike, damaging all nearby enemies and returning Quinn to the battlefield.

    • Fiora

    Fiora is still the game's most dominant top laner even after her last set of nerfs, so we're back for one more round. We don't want to take down her explosive ultimate any further, so we're just going for a generic damage nerf.

    W - Riposte

  • Bonus Attack Damage: 15 / 20 / 25 / 30 / 35 ⇒ 10 / 15 / 20 / 25 / 30

    • Graves

    Graves came out swinging, being both wildly popular and arguably the game's strongest champion. We've got some feel-good changes to his animations, especially his critical strike one, and some less-feel-good nerfs as he desperately needs them. We're looking to preserve his bursty shotgunning and unique aspects as a tanky ADC, so that means we simply have to reduce his sustained damage.

    Base Stats

  • Basic Attack and Critical Attack Animations: Sped up
  • Base Attack Damage: 54.1 ⇒ 50
  • Attack Damage per Level: 3.1 ⇒ 2.5
  • Attack Speed per Level: 2.9% ⇒ 2.5%

    • R - Collateral Damage

  • Cone Damage: 140 / 250 / 360 + 120% bonus AD ⇒ 140 / 230 / 320 + 100% bonus AD
  • Projectile Damage: Unchanged

    • Fizz

    Fizz came out right behind Graves as a super strong performer, but mostly as an AP assassin in mid lane. We want to preserve both his assassin and fighter playstyles, so we're skewing our nerfs toward his higher-AP builds. We're pulling in lighter versions of a couple of nerfs from 2013 and 2015, aimed at bringing his guaranteed burst down to size, since he has so much reliable damage already with Deathfire Grasp and 75% AP ratio Lich Bane.

    Q - Urchin Strike

  • Ability Power Ratio: 60% ⇒ 40%

    • W - Seastone Trident

  • Active Ability Power Ratio: 35% ⇒ 20%

    • Kennen

    Kennen hasn't quite reached the same heights as his other ninja compatriots and we're confident he isn't performing as well as he should. AD Kennen needs substantially more help than his other builds, so we're skewing his buffs in ways to help those players out most of all

    W - Electrical Surge

  • Passive Damage: 40 / 50 / 60 / 70 / 80% total AD ⇒ 25 / 40 / 55 / 70 / 85 + 100% bonus AD

    • Nautilus

    Unlike his other water-themed friends, Nautilus didn't come out swinging. Sometimes that anchor just weighs him down… Ultimately, he's weak in all three of his main roles (Support, Jungle, Top) and we'd like to help those latter two most of all. So we're fixing one major bug while pulling in buffs and reverting nerfs from early in his lifetime, giving him more reason to soak up experience and wade into the thick of the fight.

    Passive - Staggering Blow

  • Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where the empowered attack was critting for too much damage.

    • W - Titan's Wrath

  • Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where the shield wasn't factoring in armor or magic resistance.
  • Damage over Time: 40 / 55 / 70 / 85 / 100 + 40% AP ⇒ 40 / 65 / 90 / 115 / 140 + 40% AP
  • Shield Bonus Health Ratio: 10% ⇒ 15%
  • Shield Duration: 9.75 ⇒ 10

    • Items

    Several of our tank items are underperforming. It turns out, they've got too little health regen, so they're being increased. And we have a shop display bugfix for Banshee's Veil so you can find it when searching for health items.

    Spirit Visage

  • Health per 5: 4 ⇒ 20

    • Force of Nature

  • Health per 5: 20 ⇒ 40

    • Warmog's Armor

  • Health per 5: 10 ⇒ 30

    • Banshee's Veil

  • Stat Filter Filters: Ability Power ⇒ Health

    • Bugfixes

  • Fixed a bug where an incorrect translation was displayed in Fizz's (E) ability description in a Classic match.
  • Fixed a bug where Shyvana's Burnout (W) could be cast while it was still active.
  • Fixed a bug where Miss Fortune's Splash Art used the Classic one for the Base.
  • Fixed a bug where Shyvana’s Dragon’s Descent (R) did not cancel channels.
  • Fixed a bug where Kayle's Reckoning (Q) applied on-hit effects.
  • Fixed a bug where Graves' Classic splash art was not displayed in the Collection tab, Loading Screen, Honor Screen, Progression Screen, or End of Game Scoreboard.
  • Fixed a bug where Champions Overview Role Icons did not match the listed Champions' Roles in the Classic Collection Menu.
  • Fixed a bug where Teemo did not regain the movement speed bonus from Move Quick (W) after death.
  • Fixed a bug where Graves' overview page did not display text under "Classic Changes."
  • Fixed a bug where Nautilus' title "The Titan of the Depths" was not displayed under the champion's name.
  • Fixed a bug where Sion could lifesteal when attacking enemy Inhibitors.
  • Fixed a bug where Pantheon's Aegis Protection (P) text description contained an unlocalized string of text in the Classic Collection.
  • Fixed a bug where Quicksilver Sash, Mercurial Scimitar, or Gangplank's Remove Scurvy (W) could grant temporary vision while affected by Graves' Smoke Screen (W) Near Sighted Debuff.
  • Fixed a bug where owned Rune Pages could overflow the available content area and clip the Rune Editor or Statistics panel.
  • Fixed a bug where Classic Summoner's Spells played incorrect sound effects when cast.
  • Fixed grammatical and text formatting errors in Fiora's Classic Changes Overview and Abilities Preview tabs.

    • ARAM: Mayhem

    Hello Mayhemers!

    This patch, we're giving some champions and Augments that need a little love some extra attention. For champions, we're introducing champion-specific buffs that strengthen their core play patterns while also making them more accessible and satisfying to play in Mayhem. For Augments, we're continuing to focus on usability improvements.

    For example, Missile Split will now split when the missile reaches its end or is recast, rather than on the first target hit. We also lowered the cooldown on Triggered Inferno to show the real Samira fantasy. Let us know how these changes feel, and thank you for playing.

    See you on the Bridge!

    Champions

    Bard

  • Meep Ability Power Ratio: 50% ⇒ 67%
  • Meep Recharge: 8s ⇒ 5s
  • Meep Auto Damage per Chime Breakpoint: 6 per 3 chimes ⇒ 10 per 3 chimes

    • Garen

  • Passive Regen: 1.5%–1.01% ⇒ 2%–12%
  • W Cooldown: 22–12 ⇒ 18–12
  • W Shield Strength: 18% Bonus Health ⇒ 20% Bonus Health
  • W Passive Stacks: 0.4 per minion kill ⇒ 0.75 per minion kill

    • K'Sante

  • W Cooldown: 14–10 ⇒ 10
  • W Damage Reduction: 30% ⇒ 45%
  • E Shield Strength: 13.5% bonus health ⇒ 15% bonus health

    • Lee Sin

  • Passive Attack Speed: 40% bonus Attack Speed ⇒ 50% bonus Attack Speed
  • Passive Energy Restore: 20 / 30 / 40 ⇒ 30 / 40 / 50
  • W Shield: 60–240 ⇒ 80–320
  • Q2 Damage: 60–180 ⇒ 80–240

    • Swain

  • Damage Taken: 105% ⇒ 100%
  • Healing: 95% ⇒ 100%
  • Soul Fragments Restore: 6% flat ⇒ 3%–6% scaling with level

    • Thresh

  • Passive Soul Drop: 2 ⇒ 3
  • W Cooldown: 21 / 20 / 19 / 18 / 17s ⇒ 19 / 18 / 17 / 16 / 15s

html:
Worlds has begun, but time still passes for the rest of us non-professional mortals, so here we’ve got 26.21. This is a pretty chunky patch, with changes to some chunks like Rammus, Sion, Nunu (& Willump), as well as to a bunch of other champions across roles who’ve been on top of the game, either in presence in their role or in power. Others can have a bit more breathing room with the Worlds patch locked in, like Azir, Orianna, and Ryze. Finally, we’ve been seeing Gluttonous Greaves & Hubris overperform on ranged characters in particular, so those are getting nerfed a bit, and maybe Dawncore can work its way into some more builds with buffs.

Looking for more information on all things League of Legends? Check out our community-run wiki here!

Wrong patch notes? You can find the TFT patch notes here!

Mid-Patch Updates

October 22, 2026 Updates

Varus

This patch we did work to adjust Varus' top and bottom power skew, which involved shifting the balance between his Q and W for laning. While the resulting changes have seemed promising, we unfortunately added a major bug to his Q during this work, causing it to no longer deal reduced damage to subsequent targets. We are fixing that bug, and compensating with a buff.

  • Passive Bonus AD and AP on Kill/Takedown: (1.1 per 10% AS) as bonus AD and AP ⇒ 1.4 per 10% AS
  • Q Minimum Damage: 50 - 230 ⇒ 50 - 250

    • Patch Highlights

    Prestige True Damage Know My Name Ekko, True Damage Know My Name Akali, True Damage Know My Name Qiyana, True Damage Know My Name Senna, and True Damage Know My Name Yasuo will be available October 21, 2026.

    Replay Download Limits

    Starting during Patch 26.21, replay downloads will be limited to 10 per hour. You will still be able to download your own replays, as well as replays from your friends and other players.

    This change is necessary to prevent large-scale abuse of downloaded replays by bad actors using vibecoded apps to scrape thousands upon thousands of replays. We opted for a time-based limit to still allow creators to make content, while preventing mass exploitative downloads. We’ll continue to monitor how many replays are downloaded to ensure players have access to this important feature while preventing clear misuse.

    Champions

    Azir

    We've kept the Emperor of the Sands’ mana pool pretty dry to make sure he needs to use soldier attacks properly for lane control early instead of just spamming [Q] Conquering Sands, but this is overly restrictive now that there are strong rank up incentives on his [W] Arise! We’re buffing his Mana Growth so he can more freely use his abilities to contest lane.

    Base Stats

  • Mana Growth: 40/Level ⇒ 50/Level

    • Caitlyn

    Caitlyn’s been at a very high pick and ban rate for most players for months now despite adjustments to other marksmen and the bot meta, so it's time to nerf her. We have felt that her late-game scaling has been too strong for a while now, so we’re moving some of her power from her eyepopping full build headshots into her early game Q damage to rebalance her power curve.

    Passive - Headshot

  • Damage: 60 - 100% AD (+1% AD per 1% per Crit Chance) (+1% AD per 1% Bonus Crit Damage) ⇒ 60 - 80% AD (+0.8% AD per 1% per Crit Chance) (+0.8% AD per 1% Bonus Crit Damage)

    • Q - Piltover Peacemaker

  • Base Damage: 50 / 90 / 130 / 170 / 210 ⇒ 50 / 95 / 140 / 185 / 230

    • Darius

    Darius has moved a bit too far away from being a persistently durable damage threat that needs to be kited to more of a one shot combo playstyle. Since he has some room for power, we’re giving him a slight boost so he can swing that axe more often in sustained fights.

    Q - Decimate

  • Cooldown: 9 / 8 / 7 / 6 / 5s ⇒ 9 / 8 / 7 / 6 / 4s

    • Jinx

    Like her best friend Caitlyn, Jinx has been similarly dominant in the meta, even with the Hurricane nerf last patch. We’re slowing her roll to make it a tad harder to get her snowballing.

    Base Stats

  • Attack Damage: 59 + 3.25/Level ⇒ 59 + 3/Level
  • Health: 630 + 105/Level ⇒ 610 + 105/Level

    • Lee Sin

    Lee Sin has continued to be extremely popular since his adjustments to how his [W] Safeguard cooldown works with allies. While we like the extra flexibility that has given him, it's a bit too much power, so we’re nerfing the cooldown a bit along with a minor bug fix to how his E reveal works against invisible enemies and another small nerf to his [R] Dragon's Rage damage.

    W - Safeguard

  • Cooldown: 7s ⇒ 8s

    • E - Tempest

  • Bugfix: No longer reveals invisible enemies if they stealth after being hit by Tempest.

    • R - Dragon's Rage

  • Kick Damage: 175 / 400 / 625 (+200% bonus AD) ⇒ 150 / 350 / 550 (+200% bonus AD)
  • Collision Damage: 175 / 400 / 625 (+200% bonus AD) (+12 / 15 / 18% Kicked Champion's Health) ⇒ 150 / 350 / 550 (+200% bonus AD) (+12 / 15 / 18% Kicked Champion's Health)

    • Locke

    Locke’s been out for long enough now that we have a better picture of where he’s overly excelling and where he’s falling a bit short. Some of those areas are his extremely generous mana tuning and ability to shrug off harass, and we’re also refining his power curve by improving his scaling damage slightly, because he falls off a bit too fast if he’s not able to close out games early.

    Q - Ritual Nails

  • Unused Charge Refund: 20 - 35% mana and cooldown refund ⇒ 10 - 40% mana and cooldown refund

    • Base Stats

  • Mana Growth: 70 ⇒ 60

    • W - Soul Ignition

  • Mana Cost: 50 / 55 / 60 / 65 / 70 ⇒ 60 / 65 / 70 / 75 / 80
  • Grey Health Store Based on Current Health: 40 - 200 (both level based) ⇒ 20 - 200
  • Current Health Store: 150 - 450 (both level based) ⇒ 100 - 500 (+60% AP)

    • E - Ashen Pursuit

  • Blink Damage: 40 / 50 / 60 / 70 / 80 (+40% AP) ⇒ 40 / 55 / 70 / 85 / 100 (+50% AP)

    • Miss Fortune

    Miss Fortune has been in a relatively decent place throughout the year, but with the Hubris nerf this patch, we’re looking to compensate with a couple buffs to her damage output.

    E - Make It Rain

  • Damage: 70 / 100 / 130 / 160 / 190 (+120% AP) ⇒ 90 / 120 / 150 / 180 / 210 (+120% AP)

    • R - Bullet Time

  • Critical Strike Damage: 130% (+0.3% per 1% Bonus Crit Damage) ⇒ 145% (+0.45% per 1% Bonus Crit Damage)

    • Nidalee

    Our favorite huntress has been sitting at an extremely high winrate in high skill brackets, toeing the line into overpowered territory for some time now, even if she's not currently meta. Now that we’re bringing down the power of some other powerful meta junglers like Lee Sin, we’re giving Nidalee a minor nerf to prevent her from getting out of paw.

    W - Pounce

  • Damage: 55 / 88.75 / 122.5 / 156.25 / 190 (+50% bonus AD) (+30% AP) ⇒ 50 / 80 / 110 / 140 / 170 (+50% bonus AD) (+30% AP)

    • E - Primal Surge

  • Attack Speed: 30 / 40 / 50 / 60 / 70% ⇒ 20 / 30 / 40 / 50 / 60%

    • Nunu & Willump

    The boy and his yeti lost some power when we nerfed Hextech Rocketbelt earlier this year so that ranged mages weren't just buying it for a dash to safety, so we’re restoring some of that damage elsewhere.

    R - Absolute Zero

  • Maximum Damage: 625 / 925 / 1275 (+300% AP) ⇒ 750 / 1100 / 1450 (+300% AP)

    • Orianna

    We’re tapping up Orianna’s scalings to help her chunk a bit harder with her bread-and-butter combo in the late game without giving too much additional power to her laning phase.

    Q - Command: Attack

  • Damage: 60 / 90 / 120 / 150 / 180 (+55% AP) ⇒ 60 / 90 / 120 / 150 / 180 (+60% AP)

    • W - Command: Dissonance

  • Damage: 70 / 110 / 150 / 190 / 230 (+80% AP) ⇒ 70 / 110 / 150 / 190 / 230 (+85% AP)

    • Qiyana

    Damage on Qiyana's Q turned out to be a lot more impactful than we anticipated, so we’re partially reverting the buff we gave her back in 26.17.

    Q - Elemental Wrath / Edge of Ixtal

  • Damage: 80 / 110 / 140 / 170 / 200 (+90% bonus AD) ⇒ 70 / 100 / 130 / 160 / 190 (+90% bonus AD)

    • Rammus

    While Nidalee's winrate has been borderline overpowered in the high skill levels, Rammus has been rolling over pretty much everyone else, so he’s getting a light nerf too, ok?

    W - Defensive Ball Curl

  • Bonus Armor: 27 / 32 / 37 / 42 / 47 (+30 - 60% Armor) ⇒ 25 / 30 / 35 / 40 / 45 (+30 - 50% Armor)
  • Bonus Magic Resistance: 20 / 25 / 30 / 35 / 40 (+30 - 60% Magic Resistance) ⇒ 20 / 25 / 30 / 35 / 40 (+30 - 50% Magic Resistance)

    • Ryze

    After the significantly early game nerfs to Ryze in 26.19, he hasn't been rewarded enough for succeeding when he does scale, so we’re buffing that.

    Q - Overload

  • Flux Bonus Damage: 15% / 40% / 65% / 90% increased damage ⇒ 10% / 40% / 70% / 100% increased damage
  • Bonus Move Speed: 28% / 32% / 36% / 40% / 44% ⇒ 30% / 35% / 40% / 45% / 50%

    • W - Rune Prison

  • Damage: 60 / 90 / 120 / 150 / 180 (+60% AP) (+3% bonus mana) ⇒ 60 / 90 / 120 / 150 / 180 (+70% AP) (+3% bonus mana)

    • Sion

    Our favorite unstoppable juggernaut is looking rather stoppable in recent patches. We’re giving him some buffs to his baseline durability and rewarding him when he succeeds at using his ult to GET IN THERE rather than run away.

    Base Stats

  • Health: 655 + 87/Level ⇒ 655 + 95/Level

    • R - Unstoppable Onslaught

  • Damage Increase over the First 3s of Channeling: +0 - 166.67% Base Damage, 0 - 100% Ratio Damage ⇒ +0 - 200%
  • Bugfix: Tooltip now displays the correct minimum and maximum bonus AD ratios (40-120%). It displayed an incorrect Bonus AD Scaling (60%-120%). It was never actually changed in patch 25.16 beyond the tooltip.

    • Taliyah

    Taliyah is one of a handful of mage junglers, and we think she can be better supported for meta diversity. We’re buffing her [E] Unraveled Earth damage to make it more satisfying to land her CC combo.

    E - Unraveled Earth

  • Damage: 60 / 105 / 150 / 195 / 240 (+60% AP) ⇒ 70 / 115 / 160 / 205 / 250 (+70% AP)
  • Detonation Damage: 25 / 40 / 55 / 70 / 85 (+30% AP) ⇒ 30 / 45 / 60 / 75 / 90 (+30% AP)
  • Monster Damage: Deals 225% damage to monsters.

    • Taric

    We're smoothing out some of the rough edges in Taric’s kit to allow him to shine a bit more. Way back in the day, Taric’s W was adjusted to combat the popular Master Yi + Taric funnel strats. A consequence of this was that his spells would fizzle if they were cast at the same time that his bound ally became untargetable. We believe this harsh restriction to how his abilities function is no longer necessary given the existence of Role Quests, so we're partially reverting this change so that spells now work on untargetable allies, though we are still keeping an existing exemption on [E] Dazzle for champions that disappear on screen because the gameplay is too unclear (sorry, Master Yi).

    Q - Starlight’s Touch

  • Cast Behavior: Q casts when allies are untargetable will now successfully fire.

    • E - Dazzle

  • Cast Behavior: E casts when allies are untargetable will now successfully fire.
  • Tooltip: Updated to include “Dazzle will not cast from Vanished allies”.

    • R - Cosmic Radiance

  • Cast Behavior: R casts when allies are untargetable will now successfully fire.

    • Tristana

    Tristana’s early laning has devolved a bit into "Level 1 press [Q] and just auto attack to take complete control of the lane", which is a pretty low gameplay and off flavor way for her to succeed. We’re hitting her early [Q] attack speed so she’ll have to work a bit harder before jumping on her foes.

    Q - Rapid Fire

  • Attack Speed: 60 / 75 / 90 / 105 / 120% ⇒ 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 / 120%

    • Twisted Fate

    Alongside the Taric QoL changes, we’re giving Twisted Fate’s R the same treatment so he can reveal champs even if they’re untargetable at the time of activation.

    R - Destiny

  • Reveal: Now reveals untargetable units.

    • Varus

    In this set of changes, we’re mainly looking to snipe top lane Varus, where he tends to max W, unlike the more common Q max in bot. This won't bring his [Q] Piercing Arrow back up to prior Lethality Varus levels of power, but we believe it will help a lot with our ability to tune him for bot lane. As a maxed ability, it also offers more gameplay to Varus and his opponents to interact with than some more passive damage on W.

    Q - Piercing Arrow

  • Damage Calculation: Max Damage scaling, 53.33 - 240 (+80% bonus AD) to 80 - 360 (+120% bonus AD) ⇒ Min Damage scaling, 50 - 230 (+80% bonus AD) to 85 - 391 (+136% bonus AD)
  • Damage Increase over Channel Time: Up to 50% ⇒ Up to 70%

    • W - Blighted Quiver

  • On-Hit Damage: 4 / 13 / 22 / 31 / 40 (+15% bonus AD) (+25% AP) ⇒ 4 / 10 / 16 / 22 / 28 (+20% bonus AD) (+30% AP)
  • Per Stack Damage: 3 - 5% (+1.3% per 100 AP) Target Maximum Health ⇒ 2.5 - 4.5% (+1.4% per 100 AP) Target Maximum Health
  • Active Missing Health Damage: 6 - 14%, increased by up to 50% based on Q Channel ⇒ 6 - 10%, increased by up to 70% based on Q Channel
  • Basic Ability Cooldown Refund: 13% per stack, increased by up to 50% based on Q Channel ⇒ 11%, increased by up to 70% based on Q Channel

    • Vel'Koz

    Vel’Koz has been a fairly quiet pick this year, having little presence or meta impact in mid and support. We’re looking to give him a little bit of help by rewarding him for landing his combos.

    Passive - Organic Deconstruction

  • Damage: 35 - 180 (+60% AP) ⇒ 35 - 205 (+65% AP)

    • Viktor

    It’s time for the Glorious…Devolution. It seems Viktor has evolved past the point of exploitable weaknesses, so we’re opening that up a bit by making him slightly more vulnerable in early game skirmishes and across the board.

    Base Stats

  • Move Speed: 335 ⇒ 330

    • Q - Siphon Power

  • Shield: 40 - 140 (based on level) (+25% AP) ⇒ 30 - 130 (+20% AP)

    • Wukong

    Like Lee and Qiyana, Wukong has been a meta staple whirlwind of a force in the jungle for a while now. We’re looking to tap down his strength in the jungle while compensating for lane Wukong.

    Base Stats

  • Health Regeneration: 3.5 + 0.65/Level ⇒ 5.5 + 0.65/Level

    • Passive - Stone Skin

  • Armor per Stack: 6 - 10 (based on Champion Level) ⇒ 4.5 - 10 (based on Champion Level)

    • Xin Zhao

    Following Sundered Sky's nerfs, we feel like Xin Zhao has room for buffs to both his AD Bruiser and AS focused builds, so we’re helping out his scalings.

    Q - Three Talon Strike

  • Damage per Strike: 15 / 30 / 45 / 60 / 75 (+40% bonus AD) ⇒ 15 / 30 / 45 / 60 / 75 (+45% bonus AD)

    • E - Audacious Charge

  • Attack Speed Scaling: 1% per 5% bonus Attack Speed from permanent sources ⇒ 1% per 4% bonus Attack Speed from permanent sources

    • Yone

    The last changes to Yone successfully got him to start considering crit in his first item purchases, but also put him at a somewhat unsustainable power level. We are giving him a moderate nerf to bring him down a bit.

    Q - Mortal Steel

  • Damage: 25 / 50 / 75 / 100 / 125 (+110% AD) ⇒ 25 / 50 / 75 / 100 / 125 (+105% AD)

    • Zyra

    Like Vel'koz, Zyra has had relatively little impact in the meta as tanks and enchanter supports have reigned supreme. We’re giving Zyra a greener thumb this patch to help her combat the forces trampling over her plants.

    W - Rampant Growth

  • Seed Ammo Cooldown: 18 / 16 / 14 / 12 / 10s ⇒ 16 / 14.5 / 13 / 11.5 / 10s

    • Items

    Bastion Breaker

    • Classic

    While we announced that Classic will be rotating out in January, that doesn’t mean we’re done bringing back the good old days this year. This patch we’re bringing in four more ghosts from the past (or more, if you count their ultimates). We’ll also have multiple champions dropping in .22 and .23, so we’ve got a few more historic additions before everything’s all said and done. 

    We’re also reverting all of Kassadin’s nerfs this patch, so he’s back to full 90% ban rate power. And Atma’s Impaler is back to 2%, so for all you Metagolem enjoyers, now’s your time!

    Champions

      NEW   - Mordekaiser

    Mordekaiser is back with his kit from 2010-2015! Would you like to eat every single possible minion wave, plus both your and your enemy’s Wraith camps? Mordekaiser is the champion for you. All his abilities cost health, but damaging enemies generates a shield, so you can keep fighting no matter how low you go. And when it’s time to win a fight, your ultimate can turn it into a 6v4. Beat them with their own AD Carry!

    Passive - Iron Man

  • Mordekaiser converts damage dealt by his abilities into a decaying shield.

    • W - Creeping Death

  • Mordekaiser buffs an ally with a swarm of shrapnel that grants bonus armor and MR and damages nearby enemies over time.

    • E - Siphon of Destruction

    • R - Children of the Grave

    Arena

    Welcome back to another Arena patch! This time around we're making a larger set of changes with a couple of goals.

    We're looking to lower the power level of some of the strongest augments and increase the power of some of the weakest, as well as reduce the sharpness of some of the "one augment combos" so that the champions who're able to high roll with them require a little bit of extra juice to reach their potential.

    We're also looking to bring some of the champion outliers in power (both high and low) closer to the center. One of the ways we're doing that is through more non-standard changes that allow players the opportunity to use their champions in different ways, and to take advantage of different augments and items.

    Overall, we've shifted power in ways that we hope will change up the meta a bit and provide some fresh new build options and experiences.

entries.text: This patch we did work to adjust Varus' top and bottom power skew, which involved shifting the balance between his Q and W for laning. While the resulting changes have seemed promising, we unfortunately added a major bug to his Q during this work, causing it to no longer deal reduced damage to subsequent targets. We are fixing that bug, and compensating with a buff.

entries.text: Starting during Patch 26.21, replay downloads will be limited to 10 per hour. You will still be able to download your own replays, as well as replays from your friends and other players. This change is necessary to prevent large-scale abuse of downloaded replays by bad actors using vibecoded apps to scrape thousands upon thousands of replays. We opted for a time-based limit to still allow creators to make content, while preventing mass exploitative downloads. We’ll continue to monitor how many replays are downloaded to ensure players have access to this important feature while preventing clear misuse.

entries.text: We’ve shipped an improvement to how our patch launcher works. This improvement uses a software library that requires SSE 4.2, which results in us increasing our AMD minspec by one version. Please reference our article on minimum and recommended system requirements for more information: https://support.riotgames.com/en-us/league-of-legends/performance/minimum-and-recommended-system-requirements-league-of-legends
Fixed an issue where Zaahen (Q) would fail to complete if he does into Revive mid attack.
Fixed a bug where Summoner Teleport’s channel VFX was visible for enemies when cast in brush.
Fixed a bug where Titanic Hydra’s cooldown timer would not be displayed after use.
Fixed a bug where Zoe can get a 1000 damage smite from a minion drop earlier than expected.
Fixed a bug where Hail of Blades does not trigger on auto resets if the first attack was cancelled.
Fixed a bug where Nidalee’s (Q) spear damage could go through spell shields at max range.
Updated SFX to use the base skin’s ult SFX for Briar, Kled, and Sion when playing against them to improve clarity.
